Axial ratio, for any structure or shape with two or more axes, is the [ratio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ratio) of the length (or magnitude) of those axes to each other - the longer axis divided by the shorter.

ballistic conduction (ballistic transport) is the unimpeded flow (or [transport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transport_phenomena)) of [charge carrier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charge_carrier)s (usually [electron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron)s), or energy-carrying particles, over relatively long distances in a material.

Beamstrahlung (from [beam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charged_particle_beam) + [bremsstrahlung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bremsstrahlung) ) is the [radiation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radiation) from one beam of [charged particle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charged_particle)s in [storage ring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Storage_ring)s, linear or circular [collider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collider)s, namely the synchrotron radiation emitted due to the [electromagnetic field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electromagnetic_field) of the opposing beam.

Belle experiment was a [particle physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Particle_physics) experiment conducted by the Belle Collaboration, an international collaboration of more than 400 physicists and engineers, at the High Energy Accelerator Research Organisation ([KEK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KEK)) in [Tsukuba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tsukuba), [Ibaraki Prefecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ibaraki_Prefecture), [Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan).

colloid is a [mixture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixture) in which one substance, consisting of microscopically [dispersed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dispersion_(chemistry)) [insoluble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insoluble) [particle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Particle)s, is [suspended](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suspension_(chemistry)) throughout another substance.

Colossal magnetoresistance (CMR) is a property of some materials, mostly [manganese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manganese)-based [perovskite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perovskite_(structure)) [oxide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxide)s, that enables them to dramatically change their [electrical resistance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrical_resistance) in the presence of a [magnetic field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnetic_field).

consciousness causes collapse is an [interpretation of quantum mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interpretations_of_quantum_mechanics) in which [consciousness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consciousness) is postulated to be the main mechanism behind the process of [measurement in quantum mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Measurement_in_quantum_mechanics).

law of conservation of energy states that the total [energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy) of an [isolated system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isolated_system) remains constant; it is said to be [conserved](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservation_law) over time.
conserved current is a [current](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Current_(physics)), .

constant-resistance network in [electrical engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrical_engineering) is a network whose [input resistance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Input_resistance) does not change with [frequency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frequency) when correctly terminated.

constitutive equation or constitutive relation is a relation between two or more [physical quantities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physical_quantities) (especially [kinetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinetics_(physics)) quantities as related to [kinematic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinematics) quantities) that is specific to a material or [substance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matter) or [field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Field_(physics)), and approximates its response to external stimuli, usually as applied [field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Field_(physics))s or [force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Force)s.
constraint algorithm is a method for satisfying the Newtonian motion of a rigid body which consists of mass points.

constraint algebra is a linear space of all [constraint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constraint_(mathematics))s and all of their polynomial functions or functionals whose action on the physical vectors of the [Hilbert space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilbert_space) should be equal to zero.

[constructive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constructive_proof) quantum field theory is the field devoted to showing that [quantum field theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_field_theory) can be defined in terms of precise mathematical structures.

Constructor theory is a proposal for a new mode of explanation in fundamental [physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physics), developed by physicists [David Deutsch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Deutsch) and [Chiara Marletto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chiara_Marletto), at the [University of Oxford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Oxford), since 2012.

Contact tension (also known as the contact electromotive force) is a force suggested by [Alessandro Volta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alessandro_Volta) in 1800 to explain how electricity is generated in an [electric battery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_battery) or, as it was then called, the [Voltaic pile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voltaic_pile).

continent of stability is a hypothesised large group of [nuclide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclide)s with masses greater than 300 [dalton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalton_(unit))s that is stable against radioactive decay, consisting of freely flowing [up quark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Up_quark)s and [down quark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Down_quark)s rather than up and down quarks bound into protons and neutrons.

CSDA range is a very close approximation to the average [distance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Distance) traveled by a [charged particle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charged_particle) as it slows down to rest, calculated in the continuous-slowing-down approximation.

continuous spontaneous localization (CSL) model is a [spontaneous collapse model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Objective-collapse_theory) in [quantum mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics), proposed in 1989 by [Philip Pearle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_Pearle).

Continuous-time quantum Monte Carlo (CT-QMC) is a family of [stochastic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stochastic) [algorithm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algorithm)s for solving the [Anderson impurity model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anderson_impurity_model) at finite temperature.

continuous-time quantum walk (CTQW) is a [quantum walk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_walk) on a given [(simple) graph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graph_(discrete_mathematics)) that is dictated by a time-varying unitary matrix that relies on the [Hamiltonian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamiltonian_(quantum_mechanics)) of the quantum system and the [adjacency matrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adjacency_matrix).

Continuous-variable (CV) quantum information is the area of [quantum information science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_information_science) that makes use of [physical observables](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Observable), like the strength of an [electromagnetic field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electromagnetic_field), whose numerical values belong to [continuous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_continuity-related_mathematical_topics) [intervals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interval_(mathematics)).
Contour length is a term used in [molecular physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_physics).

definition: controlled NOT gate (also C-NOT or CNOT), controlled-X gate, controlled-bit-flip gate, Feynman gate or controlled Pauli-X is a [quantum logic gate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_logic_gate) that is an essential component in the construction of a [gate-based](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_circuit) [quantum computer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_computer).

CONUS (COherent Neutrino nUcleus Scattering) experiment is a research project at the commercial [nuclear power plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_power_plant) in [Brokdorf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brokdorf), Germany (see Figure 1).

convection–diffusion equation is a [parabolic partial differential equation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parabolic_partial_differential_equation) that combines the [diffusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diffusion_equation) and convection ([advection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advection_equation)) equations.

definition: Cooper pair or BCS pair (Bardeen–Cooper–Schrieffer pair) is a pair of [electrons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrons) (or other [fermion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fermion)s) bound together at [low temperatures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Low_temperatures) in a certain manner first described in 1956 by American physicist [Leon Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leon_Cooper).

Cooperative segmental mobility is a phenomenon associated with mobility of tens to a few hundreds of repeat units of a [polymer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polymer) and is important in defining the [transition between “glassy” and “rubbery”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glass_transition) state of the polymer.

coordinate vector is a representation of a [vector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vector_(mathematics_and_physics)) as an ordered list of numbers (a [tuple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuple)) that describes the vector in terms of a particular [ordered basis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ordered_basis).
coordination geometry of an atom is the geometrical pattern defined by the atoms around the central atom.

Copenhagen interpretation is a collection of views about the meaning of [quantum mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics), stemming from the work of [Niels Bohr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niels_Bohr), [Werner Heisenberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Werner_Heisenberg), [Max Born](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Born), and others.

Copernicium is a [synthetic chemical element](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synthetic_element); it has [symbol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_symbol) Cn and [atomic number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_number) 112.
cophonicity () of the A-B atomic pair is a measure of the overlap of the A and B contributions to a specific range of vibrational frequencies.

Core electrons are the [electron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron)s in an [atom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atom) that are not [valence electron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valence_electron)s and do not participate as directly in [chemical bond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_bond)ing.

Cornell potential is an effective method to account for the [confinement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Color_confinement) of [quarks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarks) in [quantum chromodynamics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_chromodynamics) (QCD).

correlation functions, often referred to as correlators or [Green's functions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green's_function_(many-body_theory)), are [vacuum expectation values](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vacuum_expectation_value) of [time-ordered](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_ordering) products of field operators.

correspondence principle is any one of several premises or assertions about the relationship between [classical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classical_mechanics) and [quantum mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics).

definition: cosmic coincidence problem is the observation that at the present epoch of the [universe's evolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expansion_of_the_universe), the energy densities associated with [dark matter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dark_matter) and [dark energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dark_energy) are of the same order of magnitude, leading to their comparable effects on the dynamics of the cosmos.

Cosmic rays or astroparticles are [high-energy particle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High-energy_particle)s or clusters of particles (primarily represented by [proton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proton)s or [atomic nuclei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_nuclei)) that move through space at nearly the [speed of light](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speed_of_light).

definition: Cosmic Ray Energetics and Mass (CREAM) is an experiment to determine the composition of [cosmic ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cosmic_ray)s up to the 10 == Funding == CREAM experiments are currently being funded by [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA).

Cosmogenic nuclides (or cosmogenic isotopes) are rare [nuclide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclide)s ([isotope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isotope)s) created when a high-energy [cosmic ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cosmic_ray) interacts with the [nucleus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_nucleus) of an [in situ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_situ) Solar System [atom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atom), causing nucleons (protons and neutrons) to be expelled from the atom (see [cosmic ray spallation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cosmic_ray_spallation)).

cosmological constant problem or vacuum catastrophe is the substantial disagreement between the observed values of [vacuum energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vacuum_energy) [density](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy_density) (the small value of the [cosmological constant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cosmological_constant)) and the much larger theoretical value of [zero-point energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zero-point_energy) suggested by [quantum field theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_field_theory).
cosmological phase transition is an overall change in the [state of matter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_of_matter) across the whole universe.

Cosmotron was a [particle accelerator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Particle_accelerator), specifically a [proton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proton) [synchrotron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synchrotron), at [Brookhaven National Laboratory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brookhaven_National_Laboratory).
Coster–Kronig transition is a special case of the [Auger process](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auger_effect) in which the vacancy is filled by an electron from a higher subshell of the same shell.

Cothenius Medal is a medal awarded by the [German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_National_Academy_of_Sciences_Leopoldina) (known as the Leopoldina) for outstanding scientific achievement during the life of the awardee.
Cothenius Medal awardees, 1864–1953 is a list of [Cothenius Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cothenius_Medal) awardees for the period between 1864 and 1953.

Cotton effect in [physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physics), is the characteristic change in [optical rotatory dispersion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_rotatory_dispersion) and/or [circular dichroism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circular_dichroism) in the vicinity of an [absorption band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absorption_band) of a substance.

definition: Coulomb barrier, named after [Coulomb's law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coulomb's_law), which is in turn named after physicist [Charles-Augustin de Coulomb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles-Augustin_de_Coulomb), is the energy barrier caused by [electrostatic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrostatic) interaction that two [nuclei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_nucleus) need to overcome so they can get close enough to undergo a [nuclear reaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_reaction) such as [nuclear fusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_fusion).

Coulomb blockade (CB), named after [Charles-Augustin de Coulomb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles-Augustin_de_Coulomb)'s [electrical force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coulomb's_law), is the decrease in [electrical conductance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrical_resistance_and_conductance) at small [bias voltage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voltage_bias)s of a small electronic device comprising at least one low-[capacitance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capacitance) [tunnel junction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tunnel_junction).
Coulomb excitation is a technique to probe the electromagnetic aspect of [nuclear structure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_structure).

Coulomb operator, named after [Charles-Augustin de Coulomb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles-Augustin_de_Coulomb), is a [quantum mechanical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics) [operator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operator_(mathematics)) used in the field of [quantum chemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_chemistry).

Coulomb scattering state in [quantum mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics) (a fundamental [theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_theory) in [physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physics)), describes a state of a [particle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Particle_physics) where the particle is subject to [Coulomb potential](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_potential) and is not localized to a finite region of space.

Counterfactual quantum computation is a method of inferring the result of a computation without actually running a [quantum computer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_computing) otherwise capable of actively performing that computation.

counting efficiency is the ratio between the number of [particle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elementary_particle)s or [photons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photons) counted with a [radiation counter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geiger_counter) and the number of particles or photons of the same type and energy emitted by the radiation source.
Coupled cluster (CC) is a numerical technique used for describing [many-body system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Many-body_system)s.

coupling constant or gauge coupling parameter (or, more simply, a coupling) is a number that determines the strength of the [force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Force) exerted in an [interaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fundamental_interaction).

Coupling loss, also known as connection loss, is the loss that occurs when [energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy) is transferred from one [circuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrical_circuit), circuit element, or medium to another.

Courant–Snyder parameters (frequently referred to as Twiss parameters or CS parameters) are a set of quantities used to describe the distribution of positions and velocities of the particles in a beam.

definition: [covariant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Covariance_and_contravariance_of_vectors) formulation of [classical electromagnetism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classical_electromagnetism) refers to ways of writing the laws of classical electromagnetism (in particular, [Maxwell's equations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxwell's_equations) and the [Lorentz force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lorentz_force)) in a form that is manifestly invariant under [Lorentz transformation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lorentz_transformation)s, in the formalism of [special relativity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_relativity) using rectilinear [inertial coordinate system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inertial_frame)s.

CP violation is a violation of CP-symmetry (or charge conjugation parity symmetry): the combination of [C-symmetry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C-symmetry) ([charge conjugation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charge_(physics)) symmetry) and [P-symmetry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parity_(physics)) ([parity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parity_(physics)) symmetry).

Charge, parity, and time reversal symmetry is a fundamental [symmetry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symmetry_in_physics) of [physical law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physical_law)s under the simultaneous [transformation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformation_(mathematics))s of [charge conjugation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charge_conjugation) (C), [parity transformation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parity_transformation) (P), and [time reversal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T-symmetry) (T).

Crazing is a [yielding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yield_(engineering)) mechanism in [polymer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polymer)s characterized by the formation of a fine network of microvoids and fibrils.

Creation operators and annihilation operators are [mathematical operators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operator_(mathematics)) that have widespread applications in [quantum mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics), notably in the study of [quantum harmonic oscillator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_harmonic_oscillator)s and many-particle systems.

creep (sometimes called cold flow) is the tendency of a solid material to undergo slow [deformation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deformation_(physics)) while subject to persistent mechanical [stresses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stress_(mechanics)).
critical mass is a sufficient number of adopters of a new idea, technology or innovation in a social system so that the rate of adoption becomes self-sustaining and creates further growth.
criticality or critical state is the state in which a [nuclear chain reaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_chain_reaction) is self-sustaining but not growing.

definition: cross section is a measure related to the probability that a specific process will take place in a collision of two particles.
Cross-entropy benchmarking (XEB) is a statistical measure used to evaluate the performance in [random circuit sampling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_random_circuits) experiments.

Cross-phase modulation (XPM) is a [nonlinear optical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nonlinear_optics) effect where one wavelength of light can affect the phase of another wavelength of light through the optical [Kerr effect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerr_effect).

Cross-polarized wave (XPW) generation is a [nonlinear optical process](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nonlinear_optics) that can be classified in the group of frequency degenerate ([four-wave mixing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Four-wave_mixing)) processes.
crossing is the property of [scattering amplitude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scattering_amplitude)s that allows antiparticles to be interpreted as particles going backwards in time.
Crowd simulation is the process of simulating the movement (or ) of a large number of entities or characters.

cryomodule is a section of a modern [particle accelerator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Particle_accelerator) composed of [superconducting RF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superconducting_Radio_Frequency) (SRF) acceleration [cavities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microwave_cavity), which need very low [operating temperature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operating_temperature)s (often around 2 [Kelvin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelvin)).
cryophorus is a glass container containing [liquid water](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liquid_water) and [water vapor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water_vapor).

Crystal Ball function, named after the [Crystal Ball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crystal_Ball_(detector)) Collaboration (hence the capitalized initial letters), is a [probability density function](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Probability_density_function) (PDF) commonly used to model various lossy processes in [high-energy physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High-energy_physics) such as [Bremsstrahlung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bremsstrahlung) by electrons.

crystal field theory (CFT) describes the breaking of [degeneracies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Degenerate_energy_levels) of electron [orbital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_orbital) states, usually d or f orbitals, due to a static electric field produced by a surrounding charge distribution (anion neighbors).

Crystal optics is the branch of [optics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optics) that describes the behaviour of [light](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Light) in [anisotropic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anisotropic) media, that is, media (such as [crystal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crystal)s) in which light behaves differently depending on which direction the light is [propagating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wave_propagation).
Crystallography is the branch of science devoted to the study of molecular and [crystalline structure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crystal_structure) and properties.

curved spacetime is the mathematical model in which, with [Einstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Einstein)'s [theory of general relativity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theory_of_general_relativity), gravity naturally arises, as opposed to being described as a fundamental [force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Force) in [Newton's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isaac_Newton) static Euclidean [reference frame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reference_frame).

cuspy halo problem (also known as the core-cusp problem) is a discrepancy between the inferred [dark matter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dark_matter) density profiles of low-mass galaxies and the density profiles predicted by cosmological [N-body simulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N-body_simulation)s.

definition: Darboux transformation, named after [Gaston Darboux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaston_Darboux) (1842–1917), is a method of generating a new equation and its solution from the known ones.

Darboux vector is the [angular velocity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angular_velocity) [vector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vector_(geometric)) of the [Frenet frame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frenet–Serret_formulas) of a space curve.

Darboux's theorem is a [theorem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theorem) providing a normal form for special classes of [differential 1-forms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Differential_forms), partially generalizing the [Frobenius integration theorem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frobenius_integration_theorem).

Darcy's law is an equation that describes the [flow of a fluid through a porous medium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fluid_flow_through_porous_media) and through a [Hele-Shaw cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hele-Shaw_flow).
dark energy is a proposed form of [energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy) that affects the [universe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universe) on its largest scales.

dark photon (also hidden, heavy, para-, or secluded photon) is a hypothetical [hidden sector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hidden_sector) [particle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elementary_particle), proposed as a [force carrier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Force_carrier) similar to the [photon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photon) of [electromagnetism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electromagnetism) but potentially connected to [dark matter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dark_matter).

dark star is a theoretical object compatible with [Newtonian mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newtonian_mechanics) that, due to its large mass, has a surface [escape velocity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Escape_velocity) that equals or exceeds the [speed of light](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speed_of_light).
dark state refers to a state of an atom or [molecule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecule) that cannot absorb (or emit) photons.

dark-energy star is a hypothetical compact [astrophysical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astrophysical) object, which a minority of physicists think might constitute an alternative explanation for observations of astronomical [black hole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_hole) candidates.

Darkon is a hypothetical scalar [unparticle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unparticle_physics) to introduce to the [Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minimal_Supersymmetric_Standard_Model), a [dark matter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dark_matter) candidate.

DARPA Quantum Network (2002–2007) was the world's first [quantum key distribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_key_distribution) (QKD) network, operating 10 optical nodes across [Boston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston) and [Cambridge, Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cambridge,_Massachusetts).

Dawes' limit is a [formula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_formula) to express the maximum [resolving power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angular_resolution) of a [microscope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microscope) or [telescope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telescope).

Daylight redirecting film (DRF) is a thin, flexible plastic film which can be applied to a window to refract or reflect incoming light upwards so that the deeper parts of the room are lit more evenly.

De Donder–Weyl theory is a generalization of the [Hamiltonian formalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamiltonian_formalism) in the [calculus of variations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calculus_of_variations) and [classical field theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classical_field_theory) over [spacetime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spacetime) which treats the space and time coordinates on equal footing.

de Sitter effect was described by [Willem de Sitter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willem_de_Sitter) in 1913 [[Category:Physics experiments]] [[Category:1913 in science]] 4vz3rmx527hoagcjyp9ecz3erduh83i

de Sitter invariant special relativity is the speculative idea that the fundamental [symmetry group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symmetry_group) of [spacetime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spacetime) is the [indefinite orthogonal group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indefinite_orthogonal_group) SO(4,1), that of [de Sitter space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Sitter_space).
dead time is the time after each event during which the system is not able to record another event.

death ray or death beam is a theoretical [particle beam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Particle_beam) or [electromagnetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electromagnetic_radiation) weapon first theorized around the 1920s and 1930s.

definition: Debye–Hückel theory was proposed by [Peter Debye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Debye) and [Erich Hückel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erich_Hückel) as a theoretical explanation for departures from ideality in solutions of [electrolyte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrolyte)s and [plasma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plasma_(physics))s.

Debye–Waller factor (DWF), named after [Peter Debye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Debye) and [Ivar Waller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivar_Waller), is used in [condensed matter physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Condensed_matter_physics) to describe the attenuation of [x-ray scattering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X-ray_scattering) or coherent [neutron scattering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neutron_scattering) caused by thermal motion.
decay energy is the [energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy) change of a nucleus having undergone a [radioactive decay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radioactive_decay).

decay product (also known as a daughter product, daughter isotope, radio-daughter, or daughter nuclide) is the remaining [nuclide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclide) left over from [radioactive decay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radioactive_decay).
decay scheme of a [radioactive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radioactive_decay) substance is a graphical presentation of all the transitions occurring in a decay, and of their relationships.

decoherence-free subspace (DFS) is a [subspace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linear_subspace) of a [quantum system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_system)'s [Hilbert space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilbert_space) that is [invariant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invariant_(mathematics)) to non-[unitary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unitarity_(physics)) dynamics.

Decorrelation is a general term for any process that is used to reduce [autocorrelation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autocorrelation) within a signal, or [cross-correlation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross-correlation) within a set of signals, while preserving other aspects of the signal.

Deep inspiration breath-hold (DIBH) is a method of delivering [radiotherapy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radiotherapy) while limiting [radiation exposure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exposure_(radiation)) to the heart and lungs.
defocus is the [aberration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aberration_in_optical_systems) in which an image is simply out of [focus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Focus_(optics)).

deformation quantization roughly amounts to finding a ([quantum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_algebra)) algebra whose classical limit is a given (classical) algebra such as a [Lie algebra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lie_algebra) or a [Poisson algebra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poisson_algebra).

Dejan Milošević (born in [Sarajevo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarajevo), [Bosnia and Herzegovina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bosnia_and_Herzegovina)) is a Bosnian [theoretical physicist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theoretical_physicist) and a professor of [theoretical physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theoretical_physics) since 1999 at the [University of Sarajevo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Sarajevo).

scattering, the deflection of high-energy photons in the Coulomb field of nuclei as a consequence of vacuum polarization, was observed in 1975.

delta potential is a [potential well](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potential_well) mathematically described by the [Dirac delta function](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirac_delta_function) - a [generalized function](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generalized_function).
delta prism is an optical element providing a compact folded form of the [Dove prism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dove_prism).

demon algorithm is a [Monte Carlo method](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monte_Carlo_method) for efficiently sampling members of a [microcanonical ensemble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microcanonical_ensemble) with a given energy.

Depth of focus is a [lens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lens_(optics)) [optics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optics) concept that measures the tolerance of placement of the image-capturing plane (the plane of an image sensor or a [film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photographic_film) in a camera) in relation to the lens.

Derrick Samuel Frederick Crothers (born 24 June 1942 in [Belfast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belfast), died 15 January 2021) was a [Northern Irish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Ireland) [mathematician](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematician), [physicist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physicist) and former [politician](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Politician).

definition: desert refers to a theorized gap in energy scales, between approximately the electroweak energy scale–conventionally defined as roughly the vacuum expectation value or VEV of the [Higgs field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Higgs_field) (about 246 [GeV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gigaelectronvolt))–and the [GUT scale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GUT_scale), in which no known interactions appear.

DESY (acronym for Deutsches Elektronen-Synchrotron or German [Electron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron) [Synchrotron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synchrotron)) was the first [particle accelerator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Particle_accelerator) of the [DESY](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DESY) research centre in [Hamburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamburg) and the one that gave the research centre its name.

definition: Deutsch–Jozsa algorithm is a [deterministic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deterministic_algorithm) [quantum algorithm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_algorithm) proposed by [David Deutsch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Deutsch) and [Richard Jozsa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Jozsa) in 1992 with improvements by [Richard Cleve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Cleve), [Artur Ekert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artur_Ekert), Chiara Macchiavello, and [Michele Mosca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michele_Mosca) in 1998.

Devitrification is the process of [crystallization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crystallization) in a formerly crystal-free ([amorphous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amorphous)) [glass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glass).
Dewar reactivity number, also known as Dewar number, is a measure of the reactivity in [aromatic system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aromaticity)s.

Dexter electron transfer (also called Dexter electron exchange and Dexter energy transfer) is a [fluorescence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fluorescence) [quenching mechanism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quenching_(fluorescence)) in which an [excited](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Excited_state) [electron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron) is transferred from one [molecule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecule) (a [donor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron_donor)) to a second molecule (an [acceptor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron_acceptor)) via a [non radiative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-radiative_recombination) path.

Dokshitzer–Gribov–Lipatov–Altarelli–Parisi (DGLAP) evolution equations are equations in [quantum chromodynamics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_chromodynamics) (QCD) describing the variation of [parton distribution functions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parton_distribution_function) with varying energy scales.

Dvali–Gabadadze–Porrati (DGP) model is a model of [gravity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gravity) proposed by [Gia Dvali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gia_Dvali), [Gregory Gabadadze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gregory_Gabadadze), and [Massimo Porrati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massimo_Porrati) in 2000.
Di-positronium, or dipositronium, is an [[Exotic_atom#Exotic_molecules|exotic molecule]] consisting of two atoms of [positronium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Positronium).
diagrammatic Monte Carlo method is based on stochastic summation of [Feynman diagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feynman_diagram)s with controllable error bars.

Diamond Light Source (or just Diamond) is the UK's national [synchrotron light source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synchrotron_light_source) science facility located at the [Harwell Science and Innovation Campus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harwell_Science_and_Innovation_Campus) in [Oxfordshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxfordshire).

diamond norm, also known as completely bounded trace norm, is a [norm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norm_(mathematics)) on the space of [quantum operation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_operation)s, or more generally on any linear map that acts on complex matrices.

Diamond turning is [turning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turning) using a [cutting tool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cutting_tool_(machining)) with a [diamond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diamond) tip.

dichroic material refers to: * a material which causes [visible light](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visible_light) to be split up into two distinct beams of different [wavelength](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wavelength)s ([colour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colour)s), one of which is reflected and one of which is transmitted (not to be confused with [dispersion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dispersion_(optics))), or * a material in which light rays having different [polarization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polarization_(waves)) directions are absorbed differently.

Dicke model is a fundamental model of [quantum optics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_optics), which describes the interaction between [light](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Light) and [matter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matter).
die swell (also called extrudate swell or the Barus effect) is what happens when a polymer melt comes out of an extrusion die wider than the opening it just passed through.
Dielectric wireless receiver is a type of [radiofrequency receiver front-end](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RF_front_end) featuring a complete absence of electronic circuitry and metal interconnects.
diffeomorphism is an [isomorphism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isomorphism) of [differentiable manifold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Differentiable_manifold)s.

Differential dynamic microscopy (DDM) is an imaging-based optical technique that enables performing [light scattering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Light_scattering)-like experiments by means of a conventional [optical microscope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_microscope).

Differential static light scatter (DSLS) is a term coined to represent the change in total [light scatter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Light_scattering) of a system over time or temperature in a static environment.

Diffraction-limited storage rings (DLSR), or ultra-low emittance storage rings, are [synchrotron light source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synchrotron_light_source)s where the [emittance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beam_emittance) of the electron-beam in the storage ring is smaller or comparable to the emittance of the x-ray photon beam they produce at the end of their [insertion devices](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insertion_devices).

Diffuse [reflectance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reflectance) spectroscopy, or diffuse reflection spectroscopy, is a subset of [absorption spectroscopy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absorption_spectroscopy).

diffuse series is a series of [spectral line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spectral_line)s in the atomic [emission spectrum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emission_spectrum) caused when electrons jump between the lowest p orbital and d orbitals of an atom.
Diffusion Monte Carlo (DMC) or diffusion quantum Monte Carlo otherwise the Green's function is inaccurate.

Diffusive–thermal instability or thermo–diffusive instability is an [[Combustion instability#Classification of combustion instabilities|intrinsic flame instability]] that occurs both in [premixed flame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premixed_flame)s and in [diffusion flame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diffusion_flame)s and arises because of the difference in the diffusion coefficient values for the fuel and heat transport, characterized by non-unity values of [Lewis number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lewis_number)s.
diffuson is a disorder-averaged electron-hole [propagator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Propagator), a mathematical object which often appears in the theory of disordered electronic systems.
DigitalOptics Corporation (DOC) is a [San Jose, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Jose,_California)-based technology company that designs and manufactures imaging systems for smartphones.

dihydrogen bond is a kind of [hydrogen bond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrogen_bond), an interaction between a [metal hydride](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metal_hydride) bond and an OH or NH group or other [proton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proton) donor.

dijet event is a collision between [subatomic particle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subatomic_particle)s that produces two [particle jet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Particle_jet)s.

dimension of a [vector space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vector_space) V is the [cardinality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinality) (i.e., the number of vectors) of a [basis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basis_(linear_algebra)) of V over its base [field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Field_(mathematics)).
dimensional deconstruction is a method to construct 4-dimensional theories that behave as higher-dimensional theories in a certain range of higher energies.

dimensional reduction refers to the description of a system in D spacetime dimensions in terms of an exact or [effective action](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Effective_field_theory) in fewer than D dimensions.

dimensional regularization is a method introduced by [Juan José Giambiagi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_José_Giambiagi) and [Carlos Guido Bollini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Guido_Bollini) .

dimensional transmutation is a physical mechanism providing a linkage between a [dimensionless](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dimensionless) parameter and a [dimensionful](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dimensionful) parameter.

dipole magnet is the simplest type of [magnet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnet).

Dirac matter refers to a class of [condensed matter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Condensed_matter) systems which can be effectively described by the [Dirac equation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirac_equation).

definition: Dirac membrane is a model of a charged [membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Membrane) introduced by [Paul Dirac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Dirac) in 1962.

Dirac operator is a first-order [differential operator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Differential_operator) that is a formal square root, or [half-iterate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-iterate), of a second-order differential operator such as a [Laplacian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laplacian).

Dirac spinor is a mathematical construction that is used to describe some of the [fundamental particle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fundamental_particle)s of [nature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nature), including [quark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quark)s and [electron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron)s.

Dirac–Kähler equation, also known as the Ivanenko–Landau–Kähler equation, is the geometric analogue of the [Dirac equation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirac_equation) that can be defined on any [pseudo-Riemannian manifold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pseudo-Riemannian_manifold) using the [[Laplace–Beltrami operator#Laplace–de Rham operator|Laplace–de Rham operator]].
Direct detection of dark matter is the science of attempting to directly measure [dark matter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dark_matter) collisions in Earth-based experiments.

direction cosines (or directional cosines) of a [vector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclidean_vector) are the [cosine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cosine)s of the angles between the vector and the three positive coordinate axes.

Dirk (Dik) Bouwmeester (born 1967) is a [Dutch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_people) experimental [physicist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physicist) specializing in [quantum optics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_optics) and [quantum information](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_information).

discovery of the neutron and its properties was central to the extraordinary developments in [atomic physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_physics) in the first half of the 20th century.

discrete dipole approximation (DDA), also known as the coupled dipole approximation, is a numerical method for computing the scattering and absorption of electromagnetic radiation by particles of arbitrary shape and composition.
discrete symmetry is a [symmetry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symmetry) that describes non-continuous changes in a system.
disgregation is an early formulation of the concept of [entropy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entropy).
Dislocation avalanches are rapid discrete events during plastic deformation, in which defects are reorganized collectively.

dispersive prism is an [optical prism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prism_(optics)) that is used to [disperse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dispersion_(optics)) [light](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Light), that is, to separate light into its [spectral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continuous_spectrum) components (the [color](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Color)s of the [rainbow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rainbow)).

Dissociative adsorption is a process in which a molecule [adsorbs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adsorption) onto a surface and simultaneously dissociates into two or more fragments.

definition: distance (or perpendicular distance) from a point to a line is the shortest [distance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclidean_distance) from a fixed [point](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Point_(geometry)) to any point on a fixed infinite [line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Line_(mathematics)) in [Euclidean geometry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclidean_geometry).
distortion is the alteration of the original shape (or other characteristic) of a [signal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Signal).
distortion is a deviation from [rectilinear projection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rectilinear_projection); a projection in which straight lines in a scene remain straight in an image.

Distributed temperature sensing systems (DTS) are [optoelectronic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optoelectronic) devices which measure temperatures by means of [optical fibres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_fibres) functioning as linear [sensors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sensors).

Dorothea Jameson (November 16, 1920 – April 12, 1998) was an American [cognitive psychologist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognitive_psychologist) who greatly contributed to the field of [color](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Color_vision) and [vision](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visual_perception).
dose measurements are taken by a radiation detector in order to characterise the radiation beams from medical [linear accelerators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linear_accelerators).

dose-fractionation theorem for [tomographic imaging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomographic_imaging) is a [statement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statement_(logic)) that says the total dose required to achieve [statistical significance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statistical_significance) for each [voxel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voxel) of a computed [3D reconstruction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3D_reconstruction) is the same as that required to obtain a single [2D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Two-dimensional_space) image of that isolated voxel at the same level of statistical significance.

Radiation dosimetry in the fields of [health physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_physics) and [radiation protection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radiation_protection) is the measurement, calculation and assessment of the [ionizing radiation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ionizing_radiation) dose absorbed by an object, usually the human body.

Double copy theory is a theory in [theoretical physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theoretical_physics), specifically in [quantum gravity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_gravity), that hypothesizes a [perturbative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perturbative) [duality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duality_(mathematics)) between [gauge theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gauge_theory) and [gravity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gravity).

Double electron capture is a type of [double beta decay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double_beta_decay), a permissible [decay mode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decay_mode) of an [atomic nucleus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_nucleus).

Double field theory in [theoretical physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theoretical_physics) refers to formalisms that capture the [T-duality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T-duality) property of [string theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/String_theory) as a manifest [symmetry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symmetry) of a [field theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Field_theory_(physics)).
double group was introduced by [Hans Bethe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hans_Bethe) for the quantitative treatment of [magnetochemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnetochemistry).

double pendulum, also known as a chaotic pendulum, is a [pendulum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pendulum) with another pendulum attached to its end, forming a complex [physical system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physical_system) that exhibits rich [dynamic behavior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dynamical_systems) with a [strong sensitivity to initial conditions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Butterfly_effect).

double scaling limit is a [limit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limit_(mathematics)) in which the [coupling constant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coupling_constant) is sent to zero while another quantity is sent to zero or infinity at the same moment.
Double-blind frequency-resolved optical gating (double-blind FROG) is a method for simultaneously measuring two unknown [ultrashort laser pulses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultrashort_pulse).

double-exchange mechanism is a type of a [[Ferromagnetism#Exchange interaction|magnetic exchange]] that may arise between ions in different [oxidation states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxidation_states).

double-well potential is one of a number of [quartic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quartic_function) potentials for the exploration of various physical phenomena or mathematical properties since it permits in many cases explicit calculation without over-simplification.

electromagnetic wave equation is a second-order [partial differential equation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partial_differential_equation) that describes the propagation of [electromagnetic wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electromagnetic_wave)s through a [medium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medium_(optics)) or in a [vacuum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vacuum).

Electromagnetically induced grating (EIG) is an optical [interference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interference_(wave_propagation)) phenomenon where an [interference pattern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interference_pattern) is used to build a dynamic spatial [diffraction grating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diffraction_grating) in matter.

electromechanical coupling coefficient is a numerical measure of the conversion [efficiency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy_conversion_efficiency) between [electrical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrical) and [acoustic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acoustics) energy in [piezoelectric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piezoelectric) materials.

electron bifurcation (EB) refers to a system that enables an unfavorable ([endergonic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endergonic)) transformation by coupling to a favorable ([exergonic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exergonic)) transformation.

definition: electron configuration is the [distribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Distribution_(mathematics)) of [electron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron)s of an [atom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atom) or [molecule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecule) (or other physical structure) in [atomic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_orbital) or [molecular orbital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_orbital)s.

Electron cooling () is a method to shrink the [emittance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beam_emittance) (size, [divergence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Divergence), and energy spread) of a [charged particle beam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charged_particle_beam) without removing particles from the beam.

Electron cyclotron resonance (ECR) is a phenomenon observed in [plasma physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plasma_physics), [condensed matter physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Condensed_matter_physics), and [accelerator physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accelerator_physics).

Electron diffraction is a generic term for phenomena associated with changes in the direction of [electron beams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron_beams) due to [elastic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elastic_collision) interactions with [atoms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atoms).

electron gun (also called electron emitter) is an electrical component in some [vacuum tube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vacuum_tube)s that produces a narrow, [collimated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collimation) [electron beam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron_beam) that has a precise [kinetic energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinetic_energy).

electron hole (often simply called a hole) is a [quasiparticle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quasiparticle) denoting the lack of an electron at a position where one could exist in an [atom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atom) or [atomic lattice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crystal_structure).

electron microscope is a [microscope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microscope) that uses a beam of [electron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron)s as a source of illumination.
Electron nuclear double resonance (ENDOR) is a magnetic resonance technique for elucidating the molecular and electronic structure of paramagnetic species.
Electron optics is a mathematical framework for the calculation of electron trajectories in the presence of [electromagnetic field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electromagnetic_field)s.

electron pair or Lewis pair consists of two [electron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron)s that occupy the same [atomic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_orbital) or [molecular orbital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_orbital) but have opposite [spins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin_(physics)).

Electron therapy or electron beam therapy (EBT) is a kind of [external beam radiotherapy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/External_beam_radiotherapy) where [electrons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrons) are directed to a [tumor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tumor) site for medical treatment of cancer.

Electron wake is the disturbance left after a high-energy [charged particle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charged_particle) passes through condensed matter or [plasma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plasma_(physics)).

electron-cloud effect is a phenomenon that occurs in [particle accelerators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Particle_accelerators) and reduces the quality of the [particle beam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Particle_beam).
Electron-hole droplets are a condensed phase of [exciton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exciton)s in [semiconductor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semiconductor)s.

electron-on-helium qubit is a [quantum bit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qubit) for which the [orthonormal basis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orthonormal_basis) states |0⟩ and |1⟩ are defined by quantized motional states or alternatively the spin states of an electron trapped above the surface of [liquid helium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liquid_helium).

electron-refractive effect, also known as electron induced permittivity modification (EIPM), is an [electro-optic effect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electro-optic_effect) observed in some crystals and amorphous materials, such as [chalcogenide glass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chalcogenide_glass)es and [oxides](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxides), where the [permittivity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Permittivity) reduces or increases when the material is illuminated by high energy electrons, typically from a [transmission electron microscope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transmission_electron_microscope) or [scanning electron microscope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scanning_electron_microscope).

Electronic entropy is the [entropy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entropy) of a system attributable to electrons' probabilistic occupation of states.

electronic specific heat, sometimes called the electron heat capacity, is the [specific heat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Specific_heat) of an [electron gas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron_gas).

definition: Fermi energy is a concept in [quantum mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics) usually referring to the energy difference between the highest and lowest occupied single-particle states in a quantum system of non-interacting [fermion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fermion)s at [absolute zero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_zero) [temperature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temperature).
Fermi gas is an idealized model, an ensemble of many non-interacting [fermion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fermion)s.

Fermi liquid theory (also known as Landau's Fermi-liquid theory) is a theoretical model of interacting [fermion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fermion)s that describes the normal state of the conduction electrons in most [metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metal)s at sufficiently low temperatures.

Fermi motion is the [quantum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics) motion of [nucleon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleon)s bound inside a [nucleus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_nucleus).

Fermi point has two applications but refers to the same phenomena ([special relativity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_relativity)): [[Category:Critical phenomena]] [[Category:Nanoelectronics]] [[Category:Condensed matter physics]] [[Category:Quantum field theory]] [[Category:Special relativity]] 6xwsi4q8kuorw31jw0528ica5apg0zs

Fermi problem (or Fermi question, Fermi quiz), also known as an order-of-magnitude problem, is an [estimation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estimation_theory) problem in [physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physics) or [engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Engineering) education, designed to teach [dimensional analysis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dimensional_analysis) or [approximation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Approximation) of extreme scientific calculations.

Fermi resonance is the shifting of the energies and intensities of absorption bands in an [infrared](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infrared_spectrum) or [Raman spectrum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raman_spectroscopy).
Fermi surface is the surface in [reciprocal space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reciprocal_space) which separates occupied electron states from unoccupied electron states at zero temperature.

Fermi's golden rule is a formula that describes the transition rate (the probability of a transition per unit time) from one energy [eigenstate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eigenstate) of a quantum system to a group of energy eigenstates in a continuum, as a result of a weak [perturbation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perturbation_theory_(quantum_mechanics)).

Fermilab Holometer, based at [Fermilab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fermilab) in [Illinois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois) was a laser [interferometer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interferometer) intended to be the world's most sensitive, surpassing the sensitivity of the [GEO600](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GEO600) and [LIGO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LIGO) systems, and theoretically able to detect [holographic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holographic_principle) fluctuations in [spacetime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spacetime).

definition: fermion is a [subatomic particle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subatomic_particle) that follows [Fermi–Dirac statistics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fermi–Dirac_statistics).

fermionic condensate (or Fermi–Dirac condensate) is a [superfluid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superfluid) [phase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phase_(matter)) formed by [fermion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fermion)ic particles at low [temperature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temperature)s.

fermionic field is a [quantum field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_field) whose [quanta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum) are [fermion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fermion)s; that is, they obey [Fermi–Dirac statistics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fermi–Dirac_statistics).

Fermi–Pasta–Ulam–Tsingou (FPUT) problem or formerly the Fermi–Pasta–Ulam problem was the apparent [paradox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physical_paradox) in [chaos theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaos_theory) that many complicated enough physical systems exhibited almost exactly [periodic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frequency) behavior – called Fermi–Pasta–Ulam–Tsingou recurrence (or Fermi–Pasta–Ulam recurrence) – instead of the expected [ergodic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ergodic_theory) behavior.

definition: ferrimagnetic material is a material that has populations of atoms with opposing [magnetic moment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnetic_moment)s, as in [antiferromagnetism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antiferromagnetism), but these moments are unequal in magnitude, so a [spontaneous magnetization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spontaneous_magnetization) remains.

ferroelectret, also known as a piezoelectret, is a [thin film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thin_film) of [polymer foam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polymer_foam)s, exhibiting [piezoelectric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piezoelectric) and [pyroelectric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyroelectric) properties after electric charging.

ferroics is the generic name given to the study of [ferromagnets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferromagnets), [ferroelectrics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferroelectrics), and [ferroelastics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferroelastics).

Ferromagnetism is a property of certain materials (such as [iron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron)) that results in a significant, observable [magnetic permeability](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnetic_permeability), and in many cases, a significant [magnetic coercivity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnetic_coercivity), allowing the material to form a [permanent magnet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Permanent_magnet).
few-body system consists of a small number of well-defined structures or [point particle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Point_particle)s.

Feynman parametrization is a technique for evaluating [loop integral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loop_integral)s which arise from [Feynman diagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feynman_diagram)s with one or more loops.

Feynman sprinkler, also referred to as a Feynman inverse sprinkler or reverse sprinkler, is a [sprinkler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irrigation_sprinkler)-like device which is submerged in a tank and made to suck the surrounding [fluid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fluid) in.

Feynman's algorithm is an [algorithm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algorithm) that is used to simulate the operations of a [quantum computer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_computer) on a [classical computer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer).

Feza Gürsey Institute ([Turkish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkish_language): Feza Gürsey Enstitüsü) is a joint institute of [Boğaziçi University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boğaziçi_University) and the [Scientific and Technological Research Council of Turkey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_and_Technological_Research_Council_of_Türkiye) (TÜBİTAK) on [physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physics) research, founded in 1983 by [Erdal İnönü](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erdal_İnönü) with the name Research Institute for Basic Sciences.
FHI-aims (Fritz Haber Institute ab initio materials simulations) is a software package for computational molecular and materials science written in [Fortran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortran).

definition: Fiber Optic cable termination is the addition of [connectors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_fiber_connector) to each [optical fiber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_fiber) in a [cable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_fiber_cable).
fiber disk laser is a [fiber laser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiber_laser) with transverse delivery of the [pump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laser_pumping) light.

fiber laser (or fibre laser in [Commonwealth English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_English)) is a [laser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laser) in which the [active gain medium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Active_gain_medium) is an [optical fiber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_fiber) doped with [rare-earth element](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rare-earth_element)s such as [erbium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erbium), [ytterbium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ytterbium), [neodymium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neodymium), [dysprosium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dysprosium), [praseodymium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Praseodymium), [thulium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thulium) and [holmium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holmium).

Fiber tapping is a [network tap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Network_tap) method that extracts signal from an [optical fiber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_fiber) without breaking the connection.

fiber-optic cable, also known as an optical-fiber cable, is an assembly similar to an [electrical cable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrical_cable) but containing one or more [optical fiber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_fiber)s that are used to carry light.
Fiber-optic filter is an [optical fiber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_fiber) instrument used for wavelength selection, which can select desired wavelengths to pass and reject the others.

fiber-optic sensor is a [sensor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sensor) that uses [optical fiber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_fiber) either as the sensing element ( have been proposed and demonstrated.

fiberscope is a flexible [optical fiber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_fiber) bundle with a lens on one end and an [eyepiece](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eyepiece) or [camera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camera) on the other.
Fibonacci anyon is a type of [anyon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anyon) which lives in two-dimensional [topologically ordered](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Topological_order) systems.

Field capacity is the amount of [soil moisture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soil_moisture) or [water content](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water_content) held in the [soil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soil) after excess water has drained away and the rate of downward movement has decreased.
field effect is the [polarization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_polarity) of a [molecule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecule) through space.

Field electron emission, also known as field-induced electron emission, field emission (FE) and electron field emission, is the emission of [electron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron)s from a material placed in an [electrostatic field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrostatic_field).

field equation is a [partial differential equation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partial_differential_equation) which determines the dynamics of a [physical field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physical_field), specifically the time evolution and spatial distribution of the field.

field-theoretic simulation is a numerical strategy to calculate structure and physical properties of a many-particle system within the framework of a [statistical field theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statistical_field_theory), like e.g.

Figuring is the process of final [polishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polishing) of an optical surface to remove imperfections or modify the surface curvature to achieve the shape required for a given application.
filament propagation is propagation of a beam of [light](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Light) through a medium without [diffraction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diffraction).

Filtered Rayleigh scattering (FRS) is a diagnostic technique which measures [velocity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Velocity), [temperature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temperature), and [pressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pressure) by determining [Doppler shift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doppler_shift), total intensity, and spectral line shape of laser induced [Rayleigh-Brillouin scattering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rayleigh-Brillouin_scattering).

fine electronic structure of a [solid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solid) are the features of the [electronic bands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_band_structure) induced by intrinsic interactions between [charge carrier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charge_carrier)s.

fine structure describes the splitting of the [spectral line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spectral_line)s of [atoms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atoms) due to [electron spin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron_spin) and [relativistic correction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_relativity)s to the non-relativistic [Schrödinger equation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schrödinger_equation).

definition: Fire Urgency Estimator in Geosynchronous Orbit (FUEGO) is a proposed method for early detection and evaluation of [wildfires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wildfires) using a system of [drones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unmanned_aerial_vehicle) and [satellites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satellites) in [geosynchronous orbit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geosynchronous_orbit) equipped with [infrared](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infrared) sensors.

black hole firewall is a hypothetical phenomenon where an observer falling into a [black hole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_hole) encounters high-energy [quanta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum) at (or near) the [event horizon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Event_horizon).

first law of thermodynamics is a formulation of the law of [conservation of energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservation_of_energy) in the context of [thermodynamic process](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thermodynamic_process)es.
first moment of area is based on the mathematical construct [[Moment (mathematics)#Central moments in metric spaces|moments in metric spaces]].

first principle is a basic [proposition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proposition) or [assumption](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axiom) that cannot be deduced from any other proposition or assumption.
First quantization is a procedure for converting equations of classical particle equations into quantum wave equations.

fissile material is material that can undergo [nuclear fission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_fission) when struck by a [neutron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neutron) of low energy.

fixed-target experiment in [particle physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Particle_physics) is an experiment in which a beam of accelerated particles is collided with a stationary target.
Fizeau experiment was carried out by [Hippolyte Fizeau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hippolyte_Fizeau) in 1851 to measure the relative speeds of light in moving water.

flash-gas is refrigerant in gas form produced spontaneously when the [condensed liquid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturated_fluid) is subjected to [boiling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evaporation).

Flat-field correction (FFC) is a [digital imaging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_imaging) technique to mitigate pixel-to-pixel differences in the [photodetector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photodetector) sensitivity and distortions in the [optical path](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_path).
flavour or flavor refers to the species of an [elementary particle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elementary_particle).

Flexoelectricity is a property of a [dielectric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dielectric) material where there is coupling between electrical polarization and a [[Deformation_(mechanics)#Strain|strain]] gradient.

flexural modulus, bending modulus, are heterogeneous combinations of two or more materials, each with different material properties, therefore their tensile, compressive, and flexural moduli usually are not equivalent.

Floer [homology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homology_(mathematics)) is a tool for studying [symplectic geometry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symplectic_geometry) and low-dimensional [topology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Topology).

Flory–Huggins solution theory is a [lattice model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lattice_model_(physics)) of the [thermodynamics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thermodynamics) of [polymer solution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polymer_solution)s which takes account of the great dissimilarity in [molecular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecule) sizes in adapting the usual [expression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expression_(mathematics)) for the [entropy of mixing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entropy_of_mixing).
Flotation of flexible objects is a phenomenon in which the bending of a flexible material allows an object to displace a greater amount of fluid than if it were completely rigid.
Flowability, also known as powder flow is a property that defines an ability of a powdered material to flow, related to [cohesion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohesion_(chemistry)).

Fluid thread breakup is the process by which a single mass of fluid breaks into several smaller fluid masses.

FLUXNET is a global network of micrometeorological tower sites that use [eddy covariance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddy_covariance) methods to measure the exchanges of [carbon dioxide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbon_dioxide), [water vapor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water_vapor), and energy between the [biosphere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biosphere) and [atmosphere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atmosphere).
fluxon is a [quantum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum) of [electromagnetic flux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flux).
