focus, also called an image point, is a point where [light rays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_(optics)) originating from a point on an object [converge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vergence_(optics)).

Folded optics is an [optical system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_system) in which the beam is bent in a way to make the [optical path](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_path) much longer than the size of the system.

Fondazione Bruno Kessler (FBK) is a research institution in the [Autonomous Province of Trento](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autonomous_Province_of_Trento) specializing in the fields of technology, innovation, the humanities and social sciences.
For all practical purposes (sometimes abbreviated FAPP) is a slogan used in [physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physics) to express a [[wikt:pragmatic|pragmatic]] attitude.

forbidden mechanism (forbidden transition or forbidden line) is a [spectral line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spectral_line) associated with absorption or emission of photons by [atomic nuclei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_nuclei), [atom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atom)s, or [molecule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecule)s which undergo a transition that is not allowed by a particular [selection rule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Selection_rule) but is allowed if the approximation associated with that rule is not made.
force carrier is a type of [particle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Particle) that gives rise to [force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Force)s between other particles.
Force Concept Inventory (FCI) is a widely validated instrument ascertaining high school and college students' conceptual understanding of fundamental conceptions of Newtonian mechanics.

force field is a [computational](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computational_chemistry) model that is used to describe the forces between atoms (or collections of atoms) within molecules or between molecules as well as in crystals.

FORM is a symbolic manipulation system.

form factor is a [function](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Function_(mathematics)) that encapsulates the properties of a certain [particle interaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fundamental_interaction) without including all of the underlying [physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physics), but instead, providing the momentum dependence of suitable matrix elements.

Forschungszentrum Jülich GmbH (FZJ; “Jülich Research Centre Limited Liability Company”) is a private company as part of [Helmholtz Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helmholtz_Association) with strong national funding that pursues interdisciplinary research in the fields of [energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy), [information](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Information), and [bioeconomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bioeconomy).

Forward scattering is the [deflection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diffraction) of [wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wave)s by small angles so that they continue to move in close to the same direction as before the scattering.

Forward Scattering Alignment (FSA) is a [coordinate system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coordinate_system) used in [coherent electromagnetic scattering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scattering) indicating direction.

Foucault pendulum or Foucault's pendulum is a simple device named after French physicist [Léon Foucault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Léon_Foucault), conceived as an experiment to demonstrate the [Earth's rotation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth's_rotation).

definition: Fredkin gate (also controlled-SWAP gate and conservative logic gate) is a computational circuit suitable for [reversible computing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reversible_computing), invented by [Edward Fredkin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Fredkin).

Free carrier absorption occurs when a material absorbs a photon, and a carrier (electron or hole) is excited from an already-excited state to another, unoccupied state in the same band (but possibly a different subband).

free electron model is a [quantum mechanical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics) model for the behaviour of [charge carrier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charge_carrier)s in a [metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metal)lic solid.
free entropy is an entropic [thermodynamic potential](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thermodynamic_potential) analogous to the [free energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thermodynamic_free_energy).

free motion equation is a [differential equation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Differential_equation) that describes a mechanical system in the absence of external forces, but in the presence only of an [inertial force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inertial_force) depending on the choice of a reference frame.

free particle is a particle that, in some sense, is not bound by an external [force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Force), or equivalently not in a region where its [potential energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potential_energy) varies.

Free spectral range (FSR) is the spacing in optical [frequency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frequency) or [wavelength](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wavelength) between two successive reflected or transmitted optical intensity maxima or minima of an [interferometer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interferometer) or [diffractive optical element](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diffractive_optical_element).
free-electron laser (FEL) is a fourth generation light source producing extremely brilliant and short pulses of radiation.

definition: Freeze thaw resistance, or freezing and thawing resistance, is the property of [solid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solid)s to resist cyclic [freezing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freezing) and [melting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melting).

frenesy is a measure of the [dynamical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dynamical_systems_theory) activity of a system's microscopic trajectories under [non-equilibrium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-equilibrium_thermodynamics) conditions.

frequency comb or spectral comb is represented by a [spectrum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spectrum_(physical_sciences)) made of discrete, stable and regularly spaced [spectral lines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spectral_lines).
Frequency domain (FD) sensor is an instrument developed for measuring [soil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soil) moisture content.

Frequency-resolved optical gating (FROG) is a general method for measuring the [spectral phase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spectral_density) of [ultrashort laser pulses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultrashort_pulse), which range from sub[femtosecond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Femtosecond) to about a [nanosecond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanosecond) in length.

friction torque is the [torque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torque) caused by the [frictional force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friction) working in [couple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Couple_(mechanics)) that occurs when two objects in contact move.

Frieda Axelrod Stahl (May 27, 1922 – October 1, 2021) was an American [historian of physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_physics) and [physics educator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physics_education) known for her work on the language of physics and for her advocacy of [women in science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women_in_science).

Friedmann Prize is a Soviet and Russian physics prize, awarded for outstanding work in [cosmology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cosmology) and [gravity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gravity), as well as [earth sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth_sciences).

fuel mass fraction is the ratio of [fuel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fuel) [mass flow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mass_flow_(physics)) to the total mass flow of a fuel mixture.
Fuel temperature coefficient of reactivity is the change in [reactivity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reactivity_(nuclear)) of the nuclear fuel per degree change in the fuel temperature.

fugacity of a [real gas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_gas) is an effective [partial pressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partial_pressure) which replaces the ideal partial pressure in an accurate computation of chemical equilibrium.
Fujikawa's method is a way of deriving the [chiral anomaly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chiral_anomaly) in [quantum field theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_field_theory).

functional decomposition is the process of resolving a [functional](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Function_(mathematics)) relationship into its constituent parts in such a way that the original function can be reconstructed (i.e., recomposed) from those parts.

Functional integration is a collection of results in [mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematics) and [physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physics) where the domain of an [integral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Integral) is no longer an ordinary region of space, but a [space of functions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Function_space).

Fundamental Fysiks Group was founded in [San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco) in May 1975 by two physicists, [Elizabeth Rauscher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_Rauscher) and George Weissmann, at the time both graduate students at the [University of California, Berkeley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Berkeley).

fundamental series is a set of [spectral line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spectral_line)s in a set caused by transition between d and f [orbitals in atoms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_orbital).
fundamental thermodynamic relation are four fundamental equations which demonstrate how four important thermodynamic quantities depend on variables that can be controlled and measured experimentally.

Furry's theorem states that if a [Feynman diagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feynman_diagram) consists of a closed loop of [fermion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fermion) lines with an odd number of vertices, its contribution to the [amplitude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scattering_amplitude) vanishes.
Anyon fusion is the process by which multiple [anyons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anyon) behave as one larger composite anyon.
Fusion splicing is the act of joining two [optical fiber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_fiber)s end-to-end.

Future Circular Collider (FCC) is a proposed [particle accelerator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Particle_accelerator) with an energy significantly above that of previous circular [collider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collider)s, such as the [Super Proton Synchrotron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Proton_Synchrotron), the [Tevatron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tevatron), and the [Large Hadron Collider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Large_Hadron_Collider) (LHC).
Förster coupling is the resonant energy transfer between [exciton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exciton)s within adjacent QD's ([quantum dot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_dot)s).

-factor (also called value) is a dimensionless quantity that characterizes the [magnetic moment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnetic_moment) and angular momentum of a whole atom, a particle, or a [nucleus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_nucleus).

Game theory on networks is a field that studies strategy in competing interest interactions among rational or adaptive players that are affected by the topology of networks.

gamma camera (γ-camera), also called a scintillation camera or Anger camera, is a device used to image gamma radiation emitting radioisotopes, a technique known as [scintigraphy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scintigraphy).

gamma ray, also known as gamma radiation (symbol ), is a penetrating form of [electromagnetic radiation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electromagnetic_radiation) arising from high-energy interactions like the [radioactive decay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radioactive_decay) of [atomic nuclei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_nuclei) or astronomical events like solar flares.
gamma ray cross section is a measure of the probability that a [gamma ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamma_ray) interacts with matter.

Gamma-ray spectroscopy is the qualitative study of the [energy spectra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy_spectra) of [gamma-ray source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamma-ray_source)s, such as in the nuclear industry, geochemical investigation, and astrophysics.
Gans theory or Mie-Gans theory is the extension of [Mie theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mie_theory) for the case of spheroidal particles.

Gap loss is a type of [signal strength](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Signal_strength) loss that occurs in [fiber optic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_fiber) transmission when the signal is transferred from one section of [fiber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_fiber) or cable to another.

gap-Hamming problem asks, if [Alice and Bob](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alice_and_Bob) are each given a (potentially different) string, what is the minimal number of bits that they need to exchange in order for Alice to approximately compute the [Hamming distance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamming_distance) between their strings.

gapped Hamiltonian is a [Hamiltonian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamiltonian_(quantum_mechanics)) for an infinitely large many-body system where there is a finite [energy gap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy_gap) separating the (possibly degenerate) [ground space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ground_state) from the first [excited states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Excited_state).
Gardner transition refers to a temperature induced transition in which the free energy basin of a disordered system divides into many marginally stable sub-basins.

Gas Dynamic Trap is a [magnetic mirror](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnetic_mirror) machine being operated at the [Budker Institute of Nuclear Physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Budker_Institute_of_Nuclear_Physics) in [Akademgorodok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akademgorodok), [Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia).

gas slug is a conglomerate of [high pressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partial_pressure) gas bubbles that forms within certain [volcano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volcano)es, the agitation of which is a driving factor in [Strombolian eruption](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strombolian_eruption)s.

gas-generator cycle, also referred to as the GG cycle, is one of the most commonly used engine cycles in [bipropellant liquid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liquid-propellant_rocket) [rocket engines.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket_engine) Propellant is burned in a [gas generator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gas_generator) (analogous to, but distinct from, a preburner in a staged combustion cycle) and the resulting hot gas is used to power the propellant pumps before being exhausted overboard and lost.

Gator is a low-background [germanium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germanium) counting facility for high-sensitivity [gamma-ray spectrometry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamma_ray_spectrometry) at the [Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laboratori_Nazionali_del_Gran_Sasso) in Italy.

Gaudin model, sometimes known as the quantum Gaudin model, is a model, or a large class of models, in [statistical mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statistical_mechanics) first described in its simplest case by [Michel Gaudin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michel_Gaudin_(physicist)).

gauge anomaly is an example of an [anomaly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anomaly_(physics)): it is a feature of [quantum mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics)—usually a [one-loop diagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One-loop_diagram)—that invalidates the [gauge symmetry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gauge_symmetry) of a [quantum field theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_field_theory); i.e.

gauge boson is a [boson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boson)ic [elementary particle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elementary_particle) that acts as the [force carrier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Force_carrier) for elementary [fermions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fermions).

gauge fixing (also called choosing a gauge) denotes a mathematical procedure for coping with redundant [degrees of freedom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Degrees_of_freedom_(physics_and_chemistry)) in [field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Field_(physics)) variables.

gauge group is a group of [gauge symmetries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gauge_symmetry_(mathematics)) of the [Yang–Mills gauge theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yang–Mills_theory) of [principal connection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principal_connection)s on a [principal bundle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principal_bundle).

gauge theory is the general study of [connections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connection_(mathematics)) on [vector bundle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vector_bundle)s, [principal bundle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principal_bundle)s, and [fibre bundle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibre_bundle)s.

Gauged supergravity is a [supergravity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supergravity) theory in which some [R-symmetry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R-symmetry) is gauged such that the [gravitino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gravitino)s ([superpartner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superpartner)s of the [graviton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graviton)) are charged with respect to the [gauge field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gauge_field)s.

gaugino is the hypothetical [fermion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fermion)ic supersymmetric [field quantum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Field_quantum) ([superpartner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superpartner)) of a [gauge field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gauge_field), as predicted by [gauge theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gauge_theory) combined with [supersymmetry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supersymmetry).

gaugino condensation is the nonzero [vacuum expectation value](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vacuum_expectation_value) in some models of a bilinear expression constructed in theories with [supersymmetry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supersymmetry) from the [superpartner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superpartner) of a [gauge boson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gauge_boson) called the [gaugino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaugino).

Gauss gun (often called a Gauss rifle or Gauss cannon) is a device that uses electromagnets and the physics of the [Newton's cradle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newton's_cradle) to accelerate a projectile.

Gaussian ensembles are specific [probability distribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Probability_distribution)s over [self-adjoint matrices](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermitian_matrix) whose entries are independently sampled from the [gaussian distribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal_distribution).

Gaussian Quantum Monte Carlo is a [quantum Monte Carlo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_Monte_Carlo) method that shows a potential solution to the [fermion sign problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Numerical_sign_problem) without the deficiencies of alternative approaches.

Gaussian state (also called a quasi-free state in [quantum field theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_field_theory)) is a specific type of mixed [quantum state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_state) of either multiple [boson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boson)s or multiple [fermion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fermion)s.

Gausson is a [soliton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soliton) which is the solution of the [logarithmic Schrödinger equation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logarithmic_Schrödinger_equation), which describes a quantum particle in a possible [nonlinear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nonlinear_system) [quantum mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics).

Hydraulic redistribution is a passive mechanism where water is transported from moist to dry soils via subterranean networks.
hydrodynamic radius of a [macromolecule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macromolecule) or [colloid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colloid) particle is ==References== * Grosberg AY and Khokhlov AR.
Hydrogen darkening is a physical degradation of the [[Glass#Optical properties|optical properties]] of [glass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glass).

hydrogen ion is an [ion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ion) created when a [hydrogen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrogen) atom loses or gains an [electron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron).
hydrogen-like atom (or hydrogenic atom) is any [atom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atom) or [ion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ion) with a single [electron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron).

Hydroxyl ion absorption is the [absorption](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absorption_(electromagnetic_radiation)) in [optical fiber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_fiber)s of [electromagnetic radiation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electromagnetic_radiation), including the near-[infrared](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infrared), due to the presence of trapped [hydroxyl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydroxyl) [ions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ions) remaining from water as a contaminant.

Hygroscopic cycle is a [thermodynamic cycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thermodynamic_cycle) converting [thermal energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thermal_energy) into mechanical [power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Power_(physics)) by the means of a [steam turbine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steam_turbine).

Hylogenesis is a [physical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physics) [theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_theory) about the mechanism behind the origins of [dark matter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dark_matter) and [antimatter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antimatter).

hypercharge (a portmanteau of [hyperon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyperon)ic and [charge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charge_(physics))) Y of a [particle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subatomic_particle) is a [quantum number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_number) conserved under the [strong interaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strong_interaction).

hypercolor is a hypothetical attractive [force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Force) that binds [prequark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prequark)s together by the exchange of [hypergluon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypergluon)s, analogous to the exchange of [gluon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gluon)s by the [color](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Color_charge) force, which binds [quark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quark)s together.
hyperdeformation is theoretically predicted states of an [atomic nucleus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_nucleus) with an extremely elongated shape and a very high angular momentum.

hyperfine structure is defined by small shifts in otherwise [degenerate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Degenerate_energy_levels) electronic [energy levels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy_levels) and the resulting [splittings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy_level_splitting) in those electronic energy levels of [atom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atom)s, [molecule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecule)s, and [ion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ion)s, due to electromagnetic multipole interaction between the nucleus and electron clouds.

hypernucleus is similar to a conventional [atomic nucleus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_nucleus), but contains at least one [hyperon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyperon) in addition to the normal [proton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proton)s and [neutron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neutron)s.

hyperpolarizability, a nonlinear-optical property of a molecule, is the second order [electric susceptibility](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_susceptibility) per unit volume.

Hyper-radial or hyperradiant Fresnel lenses are [Fresnel lens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fresnel_lens)es used in [lighthouses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lighthouses).

hypertriton is a type of [hypernucleus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypernucleus), formed of a [proton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proton), a [neutron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neutron) and any [hyperon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyperon).

Hückel method or Hückel molecular orbital theory, proposed by [Erich Hückel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erich_Hückel) in 1930, is a simple [method for calculating molecular orbitals as linear combinations of atomic orbitals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LCAO_MO_Method).

magic wavelength (also known as a related quantity, magic frequency) is the wavelength of an [optical lattice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_lattice) where the [polarizabilities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polarizability) of two [atomic clock states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_clock) have the same value, such that the [AC Stark shift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stark_effect) caused by the [laser intensity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intensity_(physics)) fluctuation has no effect on the [transition frequency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyperfine_structure) between the two clock states.

Magnetic catalysis is a physics phenomenon, which is defined as an enhancement of [dynamical symmetry breaking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dynamical_symmetry_breaking) by an external [magnetic field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnetic_field) in [quantum field theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_field_theory), used for the description of quantum ([quasi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quasiparticle)-)particles in [particle physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Particle_physics), [nuclear physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_physics) and [condensed matter physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Condensed_matter_physics).

magnetic lattice is a composition of [electromagnet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electromagnet)s at given longitudinal positions around the vacuum tube of a [particle accelerator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Particle_accelerator), and thus along the path of the enclosed [charged particle beam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charged_particle_beam).

magnetic monopole is a hypothetical [particle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Particle) that is an isolated [magnet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnet) with only one magnetic pole (a north pole without a south pole or vice versa).
magnetic photon is a [[List of particles#Hypothetical particles|hypothetical particle]].

magnetic quantum number is a [quantum number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_number) used to distinguish quantum states of an [electron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron) or other particle according to its [angular momentum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angular_momentum) along a given axis in space.

magnetic resonance is a [resonant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resonant) effect that can appear when a [magnetic dipole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnetic_dipole) is exposed to a static [magnetic field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnetic_field) and perturbed with another, oscillating [electromagnetic field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electromagnetic_field).

magnetic topological insulators are three dimensional [magnetic materials](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnet) with a non-trivial [topological index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Topological_index) protected by a [symmetry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symmetry) other than [time-reversal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T-symmetry).

magnetic trap is an apparatus which uses a [magnetic field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnetic_field) gradient to trap neutral particles with [magnetic moment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnetic_moment)s.

magneto-optical trap (MOT) is an apparatus which uses [laser cooling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laser_cooling) and a spatially varying [magnetic field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnetic_field) to create a [trap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnetic_trap_(atoms)) which can produce samples of [cold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultracold_atom) neutral [atom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atom)s.

magnetocaloric effect (MCE, from [magnet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnet) and [calorie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calorie)) is a phenomenon in which certain materials warm up when a [magnetic field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnetic_field) is applied.

Magnetocapacitance is a property of some [dielectric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dielectric), insulating materials, and metal–insulator–metal heterostructures that exhibit a change in the value of their [capacitance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capacitance) when an external [magnetic field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnetic_field) is applied to them.
magnetoelectric effect (ME) denotes any coupling between the magnetic and the electric properties of a material.

near field and far field are regions of the [electromagnetic (EM) field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electromagnetic_field) around an object, such as a transmitting [antenna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antenna_(radio)), or the result of radiation scattering off an object.

nearly free electron model (or NFE model and quasi-free electron model) is a [quantum mechanical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics) model of physical properties of [electron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron)s that can move almost freely through the [crystal lattice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crystal_structure) of a solid.

neutral particle oscillation is the transmutation of a particle with zero [electric charge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_charge) into another neutral particle due to a change of a non-zero internal [quantum number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_number), via an interaction that does not conserve that quantum number.

neutrino minimal standard model (often abbreviated as νMSM) is an extension of the [Standard Model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_Model) of particle physics, by the addition of three [right-handed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chirality_(physics)) [neutrino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neutrino)s with masses smaller than the [electroweak scale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electroweak_scale).

neutrino theory of light is the proposal that the [photon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photon) is a composite particle formed of a [neutrino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neutrino)–[antineutrino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antineutrino) [pair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pair_production).

Neutrinoless double beta decay (0νββ) is a commonly proposed and experimentally pursued theoretical [radioactive decay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radioactive_decay) process that would prove a [Majorana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Majorana_particle) nature of the [neutrino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neutrino) [particle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Particle).

Neutron capture is a [nuclear reaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_reaction) in which an [atomic nucleus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_nucleus) and one or more [neutron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neutron)s collide and merge to form a heavier nucleus.
a. BNCT is based on the neutron capture and decay reactions that occur when boron-10 is irradiated with low-energy (0.0025 eV) thermal neutrons.
neutron cross section is used to express the likelihood of interaction between an incident [neutron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neutron) and a target nucleus.

Neutron emission is a mode of [radioactive decay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radioactive_decay) in which one or more [neutron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neutron)s are ejected from a [nucleus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_nucleus).
neutron probe is a device used to measure the quantity of [water](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water) present in [soil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soil).

neutron research facility is most commonly a big laboratory operating a large-scale [neutron source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neutron_source) that provides [thermal neutron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thermal_neutron)s to a suite of research instruments.

Neutron Science Laboratory (NSL) is situated within the [[University of Michigan#North Campus|North Campus]] of the [University of Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Michigan) and houses various neutron and gamma-ray sources and a range of nuclear [radiation detection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radiation_detection_(disambiguation)) equipment.
Neutron transport (also known as neutronics) is the study of the motions and interactions of [neutron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neutron)s with materials.

neutron–proton ratio (N/Z ratio or nuclear ratio) of an [atomic nucleus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_nucleus) is the [ratio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ratio) of its number of [neutron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neutron)s to its number of [proton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proton)s.

Sir Nevill Francis Mott (30 September 1905 – 8 August 1996) was a British [theoretical physicist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theoretical_physicist) who won the [Nobel Prize for Physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_for_Physics) in 1977 for his work on the electronic structure of magnetic and [disordered](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amorphous_solid) systems, especially [amorphous semiconductors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amorphous_semiconductors).

Newton's laws of motion are three [physical laws](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physical_laws) that describe the relationship between the [motion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motion) of an object and the [force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Force)s acting on it.

Ninithi ([Sinhala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinhala_language): නිනිති) is [free and open source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_and_open_source) modelling software that can be used to visualize and analyze carbon materials used in [nanotechnology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanotechnology).

Niobium–tin is an [intermetallic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intermetallic) compound of [niobium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niobium) (Nb) and [tin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tin) (Sn), used industrially as a [type-II superconductor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Type-II_superconductor).

NNPDF is the acronym used to identify the [parton distribution functions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parton_distribution_functions) from the NNPDF Collaboration.
no-broadcasting theorem is a result of [quantum information theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_information_science).

no-cloning theorem states that it is impossible to create an independent and identical copy of an arbitrary unknown [quantum state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_state), a statement which has profound implications in the field of [quantum computing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_computer) among others.

no-communication theorem (also referred to as the no-signaling principle) is a [no-go theorem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No-go_theorem) in [quantum information theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_information).

no-deleting theorem of [quantum information theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_information_science) is a [no-go theorem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No-go_theorem) which states that, in general, given two copies of some arbitrary quantum state, it is impossible to delete one of the copies.
no-go theorem is a [theorem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theorem) that states that a particular situation is not physically possible.
no-hiding theorem denotes the fact that one may augment the unused dimension of the environment Hilbert space by zero vectors.

Nobel Committee for Physics is the [Nobel Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Committee) responsible for proposing laureates for the [Nobel Prize for Physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_for_Physics).

NOBLEX E-Optics GmbH, formerly Docter Optics, is a German manufacturer of optics, including [binoculars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Binoculars), [rifle scope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rifle_scope)s, [spotting scope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotting_scope)s, [red dot sight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_dot_sight)s, [flashlight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flashlight)s and [reading glasses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reading_glasses).

non-contact force is a [force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Force) which acts on an object without coming physically in contact with it.

non-Hermitian quantum mechanics describes [quantum mechanical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics) systems where [Hamiltonians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamiltonian_(quantum_mechanics)) are not [Hermitian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermitian_operator).

non-invertible symmetry is a [symmetry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symmetry_(physics)) of a [quantum field theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_field_theory) that is not described by a [group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Group_(mathematics)), and which in particular does not have an [inverse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inverse_element).

Non-ionizing (or non-ionising) radiation refers to any type of [electromagnetic radiation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electromagnetic_radiation) that does not carry enough [energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy) per [quantum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum) ([photon energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photon_energy)) to [ionize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ionize) atoms or molecules—that is, to completely remove an [electron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron) from an [atom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atom) or [molecule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecule).

Non-linear inverse Compton scattering (NICS), also known as non-linear Compton scattering and multiphoton Compton scattering, is the scattering of multiple low-energy [photon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photon)s, given by an intense [electromagnetic field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electromagnetic_field), in a high-energy photon ([X-ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X-ray) or [gamma ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamma_ray)) during the interaction with a [charged particle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charged_particle), in many cases an [electron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron).

non-local quantum computation (or NLQC) is a distributed method of performing a [quantum computation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_computation); the method involves shared [entanglement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_entanglement) and a single, simultaneous round of communication.

Optical conductivity is the property of a material which gives the relationship between the induced [current](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Current_(electricity)) density in the material and the magnitude of the inducing [electric field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_field) for arbitrary [frequencies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frequency).
Optical contact bonding is a glueless process whereby two closely conformal surfaces are joined, being held purely by [intermolecular forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intermolecular_forces).

optical correlator is an [optical computer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_computer) for comparing two signals by utilising the [[Fourier_optics#Fourier_transforming_property_of_lenses|Fourier transforming properties of a lens]].

optical depth or optical thickness is the [natural logarithm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_logarithm) of the ratio of incident to transmitted [radiant power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radiant_power) through a material.

definition: Optical depth in [astrophysics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astrophysics) refers to a specific level of [transparency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transparency_and_translucency).

Optical DownConverter (ODC) is an example of a [non-linear optical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-linear_optics) process, in which two beams of [light](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Light) of different [frequencies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frequency) is simply a statement that [energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy) is conserved.

definition: Optical Engineering is a monthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering research, development, and uses of [optical science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optics) and [optical engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_engineering), published by [SPIE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SPIE).

optical fiber, or optical fibre, is a flexible [glass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glass) or plastic [fiber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiber) that can transmit [light](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Light) from one end to the other.

Optical Fiber Technology is a [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) that is published by [Elsevier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elsevier) (formerly by [Academic Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academic_Press)).

optical frequency multiplier is a [nonlinear optical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nonlinear_optics) device in which [photon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photon)s interacting with a nonlinear material are effectively ==Lasers== Optical frequency multipliers are common in high-power lasers, notably those used for [inertial confinement fusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inertial_confinement_fusion) (ICF) experiments.

optical interleaver is a 3-port passive [fiber-optic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiber_optics) device that is used to combine (Mux) two sets of [dense wavelength-division multiplexing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dense_wavelength-division_multiplexing) (DWDM) channels (odd and even channels) into a composite signal stream in an interleaving way.

optical lattice is formed by the [interference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interference_(wave_propagation)) of counter-propagating [laser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laser) beams, creating a spatially periodic intensity pattern.

Optical lens design is the process of [designing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Engineering_design_process) a [lens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lens_(optics)) to meet a set of performance requirements and constraints, including cost and manufacturing limitations.

Optical Materials is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) that publishes original papers and review articles on the design, synthesis, characterisation and applications of materials, suitable for various [optical device](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_instrument)s.

Optical Materials Express is a monthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) and [open access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_access) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) published by [Optica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optica_(society)).
Optical Mechanics, Inc. or OMI is a high-end American [telescope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telescope) and optics instrument manufacturer.
optical medium is material through which [light](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Light) and other [electromagnetic wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electromagnetic_wave)s propagate.
optical modulator is a device which is used to [modulate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modulation) a [beam of light](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beam_of_light).
Optical molasses (OM) is a [laser cooling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laser_cooling) configuration that can produce extremely cold ensembles of neutral atoms.

optical parametric amplifier, abbreviated OPA, is a [laser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laser) light source that emits light of variable [wavelength](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wavelength)s by an optical [parametric amplification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parametric_amplifier) process.
optical parametric oscillator (OPO) is a [parametric oscillator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parametric_oscillator) that oscillates at optical frequencies.

Optical path (OP) is the [trajectory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trajectory) that a [light ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_(optics)) follows as it propagates through an [optical medium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_medium).

optical path length (OPL, denoted Λ in equations), also known as optical length or optical distance, is the vacuum length that light travels over the same time taken to travel through a given medium length.

optical phase space is a [phase space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phase_space) in which all [quantum state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_state)s of an [optical system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_system) are described.
optical power meter (OPM) is a device used to measure the power in an [optical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical) signal.

definition: Optical Review is a bimonthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) that was established in 1994 and is published by [Springer Science+Business Media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springer_Science+Business_Media) in partnership with the [Optical Society of Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_Society_of_Japan).

Optical Society was a [scientific society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_society) founded in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London) in 1899, which published Transactions of the Optical Society.

Optical spaces are [mathematical space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_space)s, often endowed with [coordinate system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coordinate_system)s, that facilitate the modelling of [optical system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_system)s as mathematical [transformations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformation_(function)).

optical theorem is a general law of [wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wave) [scattering theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scattering_theory), which relates the zero-angle [scattering amplitude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scattering_amplitude) to the total [cross section](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross_section_(physics)) of the scatterer.

optical time-domain reflectometer (OTDR) is an [optoelectronic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optoelectronic) instrument used to characterize an [optical fiber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_fiber).

optical transfer function (OTF) of an optical system such as a [camera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camera), [microscope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microscope), [human eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_eye), or [projector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Image_projector) is a scale-dependent description of their imaging contrast.

definition: Optical tweezers (originally called single-beam gradient force trap) are [scientific instrument](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_instrument)s that use a highly focused [laser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laser) beam to hold and move microscopic and sub-microscopic objects like [atom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atom)s, [nanoparticle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanoparticle)s and droplets, in a manner similar to [tweezers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tweezers).

optical vortex (also known as a photonic quantum vortex, screw dislocation or phase singularity) is a zero of an [optical field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_field); a point of zero [intensity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intensity_(physics)).
optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) is a technique for detecting quantum systems with [spin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin_(physics))-dependent optical transitions.

Optics is the branch of [physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physics) that studies the behaviour, manipulation, and detection of [electromagnetic radiation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electromagnetic_radiation), including its interactions with [matter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matter) and [instruments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_instruments) that use or [detect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photodetector) it.
Optics and Spectroscopy is a monthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal).

Optics Communications is a biweekly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) published by [Elsevier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elsevier).

Optics Express is a biweekly [peer-review](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-review)ed [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) published by [Optica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optica_(society)).

Optics Letters is a biweekly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) published by [Optica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optica_(society)) (formerly known as Optical Society of America).

Optics Valley is a region in southern [Arizona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona), centered on [Tucson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tucson), that is home to a high concentration of [optics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optics) companies spawned by research at the [University of Arizona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Arizona).

OPTOS (optical properties of textured optical sheets) is a simulation formalism for determining optical properties of sheets with plane-parallel structured interfaces.

orbital hybridisation (or hybridization) is the concept of mixing [atomic orbital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_orbital)s to form new hybrid orbitals (with different energies, shapes, etc., than the component atomic orbitals) suitable for the pairing of electrons to form [chemical bond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_bond)s in [valence bond theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valence_bond_theory).
orbital overlap is the concentration of [orbitals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_orbital) on adjacent atoms in the same regions of space.

definition: Orchestrated objective reduction (Orch OR) is a controversial theory postulating that [consciousness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consciousness) originates at the [quantum level](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mind) inside [neurons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurons) (rather than being a product of [neural connections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_pathway)).

order operator or an order field is a [quantum field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_field) version of Landau's [order parameter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_parameter) whose expectation value characterizes [phase transition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phase_transition)s.
Organic Rankine cycle (ORC) is a type of [thermodynamic cycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thermodynamic_cycle).

Orr–Sommerfeld equation, in [fluid dynamics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fluid_dynamics), is an [eigenvalue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eigenvalue) equation describing the linear two-dimensional modes of disturbance to a [viscous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viscosity) parallel flow.

oscillator representation is a projective [unitary representation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unitary_representation) of the [symplectic group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symplectic_group), first investigated by [Irving Segal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irving_Segal), [David Shale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Shale), and [André Weil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/André_Weil).

Oskar Klein Memorial Lecture at [Stockholm University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockholm_University), dedicated to the memory of the [Swedish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweden) [physicist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physicist) [Oskar Klein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oskar_Klein) (1894-1977), is held annually since 1988 by a prominent physicist, who also receives the Oskar Klein Medal.

Oskar Painter is a [Canadian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian) born (1972) experimental [physicist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physicist) who works on [nanoscale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanoscopic_scale) [optics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optics), [nanomechanical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanomechanics) devices, and [superconducting qubits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superconducting_qubits).

Ostrogradsky instability is a feature of some solutions of theories having [equations of motion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equation_of_motion) with more than two time [derivatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derivative_(mathematics)) (higher-derivative theories).

Otto cycle (named after [Nicolaus Otto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicolaus_Otto)) is an idealized [thermodynamic cycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thermodynamic_cycle) that describes the functioning of a typical [spark ignition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spark-ignition_engine) [piston engine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piston_engine).
Ourida Chouaki ( – 12 August 2015) was an Algerian [women's rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women's_rights) activist.
out-of-time-ordered correlator (OTOC) is the quantum [Lyapunov exponent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyapunov_exponent).
ovality or noncircularity is the degree of deviation from perfect circularity of the cross section of the core or cladding of the fiber.

photo-Carnot engine is a [Carnot cycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carnot_cycle) engine in which the working medium is a photon inside a cavity with perfectly reflecting walls.
Photo-reflectance is an [optical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical) technique for investigating the material and electronic properties of [thin film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thin_film)s.

Photoconductivity is an [optical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_phenomenon) and [electrical phenomenon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrical_phenomenon) in which a material becomes more [electrically conductive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_conductance) due to the absorption of [electromagnetic radiation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electromagnetic_radiation) such as [visible light](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visible_spectrum), [ultraviolet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultraviolet) light, [infrared](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infrared) light, or [gamma radiation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamma_rays).

Photodisintegration (also called phototransmutation, or a photonuclear reaction) is a [nuclear process](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_process) in which an [atomic nucleus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_nucleus) absorbs a high-energy [gamma ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamma_ray), enters an excited state, and immediately decays by emitting a subatomic particle.

photoelasticity describes changes in the [optical properties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_properties) of a material under mechanical [deformation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deformation_(engineering)).

photoelectric effect is the emission of [electron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron)s from a material caused by [electromagnetic radiation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electromagnetic_radiation) such as [ultraviolet light](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultraviolet_light).

definition: Photofission is a process in which a [nucleus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_nucleus), after absorbing a [gamma ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamma_ray), undergoes [nuclear fission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_fission) and splits into two or more fragments.

Photofragment ion imaging (or product imaging) is an experimental technique for making measurements of the velocity of product molecules or particles following a [chemical reaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_reaction) or the [photodissociation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photodissociation) of a parent molecule.

Protein–protein interactions (PPIs) are physical contacts of high specificity established between two or more [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) molecules as a result of biochemical events steered by interactions that include [electrostatic forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrostatic_forces), [hydrogen bond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrogen_bond)ing and the [hydrophobic effect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrophobic_effect).

Proton capture is a [nuclear reaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_reaction) in which an [atomic nucleus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_nucleus) and one or more [proton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proton)s collide and merge to form a heavier nucleus.

Proton computed tomography (pCT), or proton CT, is an imaging modality first proposed by [Cormack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allan_McLeod_Cormack) in 1963 ], Arney, Kat, Science blog, [Cancer Research UK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cancer_Research_UK), 16 September 2013 [[Category:Radiation therapy]] [[Category:Medical physics]] [[Category:Proton]] bxakeke3orplucikwsdh31ciliwgaxl

Proton emission (also known as proton radioactivity) is a rare type of radioactive decay in which a [proton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proton) is ejected from a [nucleus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_nucleus).

proton spin crisis (or proton spin puzzle) is a theoretical crisis precipitated by a 1987 experiment by the [European Muon Collaboration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Muon_Collaboration) (EMC), == References == == External links == * [[Category:Proton]] [[Category:Unsolved problems in physics]] ttnpaahgsvicehevh516pa4dl4pwahp

Proton Synchrotron Booster (PSB) is the first and smallest circular proton [accelerator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Particle_accelerator) (a [synchrotron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synchrotron)) in the accelerator chain at the [CERN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CERN) injection complex, which also provides beams to the [Large Hadron Collider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Large_Hadron_Collider).

definition: Proton tunneling is a type of [quantum tunneling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_tunneling) involving the instantaneous disappearance of a [proton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proton) in one site and the appearance of the same proton at an adjacent site separated by a potential barrier.

pseudo Jahn–Teller effect (PJTE), occasionally also known as second-order JTE, is a direct extension of the [Jahn–Teller effect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jahn–Teller_effect) (JTE) where [spontaneous symmetry breaking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spontaneous_symmetry_breaking) in polyatomic systems ([molecules](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecules) and [solids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solids)) occurs even when the relevant electronic states are not [degenerate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Degenerate_energy_levels).

pseudogap describes a state where the [Fermi surface](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fermi_surface) of a material possesses a partial [energy gap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy_gap), for example, a [band structure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_band_structure) state where the Fermi surface is gapped only at certain points.

PSF Lab is a software program that allows the calculation of the illumination [point spread function](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Point_spread_function) (PSF) of a [confocal microscope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Confocal_microscope) under various imaging conditions.
