definition: Pulse programming in the field of [experimental physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Experimental_physics) refers to engineering sinusoidal electromagnetic waveforms to have programmable frequencies, phases, and amplitudes.

pulse tube refrigerator (PTR) or pulse tube cryocooler is a developing technology that emerged largely in the early 1980s with a series of other innovations in the broader field of [thermoacoustics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thermoacoustics).

Pulsed electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) is an [electron paramagnetic resonance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron_paramagnetic_resonance) technique that involves the alignment of the net magnetization vector of the [electron spins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron_magnetic_moment) in a constant [magnetic field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnetic_field).

Pulsed power is the science and technology of accumulating [energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy) over a relatively long period of time and releasing it instantly, thus increasing the instantaneous power.
pupil function or aperture function describes how a light wave is affected upon transmission through an optical imaging system such as a camera, microscope, or the human eye.

pupil magnification of an optical system is the ratio of the diameter of the [exit pupil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exit_pupil) to the diameter of the [entrance pupil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entrance_pupil).

purity of a normalized [quantum state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_state) is a scalar defined as the IPR then gives some information about the localization in the space at consideration, e.g.

categories: Academic staff of the Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology

definition: value for a [nuclear reaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_reaction) is the amount of [energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy) absorbed or released during the reaction.
Q-ball is a type of [non-topological soliton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-topological_soliton).

q-plate is an [optical device](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_device) that can form a [light beam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Light_beam) with [orbital angular momentum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orbital_angular_momentum_of_light) (OAM) from a beam with well-defined [spin angular momentum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin_angular_momentum_of_light) (SAM).

Quark matter or QCD matter refers to matter governed by [quantum chromodynamics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_chromodynamics) and involving [quark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quark)s and [gluon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gluon)s.

QCD sum rules (or [Shifman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mikhail_Shifman)–[Vainshtein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arkady_Vainshtein)–[Zakharov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valentin_Ivanovich_Zakharov) sum rules) are a way of dealing with this.
categories: Institute for Theoretical and Experimental Physics

definition: QED vacuum or quantum electrodynamic vacuum is the [field-theoretic vacuum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vacuum_state) of [quantum electrodynamics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_electrodynamics).

QIP (which stands for Quantum Interactive Proof) is the [quantum computing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_computing) analogue of the classical [complexity class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complexity_class) [IP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IP_(complexity)), which is the set of problems solvable by an [interactive proof system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interactive_proof_system) with a [polynomial-time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polynomial-time) verifier and one computationally unbounded prover.

QMA, as an abbreviation for Quantum Merlin Arthur, refers to a [complexity class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complexity_class) in [computational complexity theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computational_complexity_theory).

QMC@Home was a [volunteer computing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volunteer_computing) project for the [BOINC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BOINC) client aimed at further developing and testing [Quantum Monte Carlo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_Monte_Carlo) (QMC) for use in [quantum chemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_chemistry).
QpiAI-Indus is the India's first full stack [quantum computer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_computing).

Quadratic gravity (QG) is an extension of [general relativity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_relativity) obtained by adding all local quadratic-in-curvature terms to the [Einstein–Hilbert Lagrangian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Einstein–Hilbert_action).
quadratic Lie algebra is a [Lie algebra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lie_algebra) together with a compatible [symmetric bilinear form](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symmetric_bilinear_form).

quadrupole or quadrapole is one of a sequence of configurations of things like [electric charge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_charge) or [current](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_current), [magnetic field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quadrupole_magnet)s, or [gravitational mass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gravitational_mass) that can exist in ideal form, but it is usually just part of a [multipole expansion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multipole_expansion) of a more complex structure reflecting various orders of complexity.

quadrupole formula describes the [gravitational wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gravitational_wave)s that are emitted from a system of masses in terms of the (mass) [quadrupole moment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quadrupole_moment).

Quadrupole magnets consist of a group of four [magnet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnet)s laid out so that in the planar [multipole expansion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multipole_expansion) of the field, the dipole terms cancel and where the lowest significant terms in the field equations are [quadrupole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quadrupole).

Quadrupole splitting is an example of a [hyperfine interaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyperfine_structure) found in [gamma-ray spectroscopy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamma-ray_spectroscopy), in the circumstance where nuclei with a non-radially-symmetric shape (that is, with a spin quantum number greater than 1/2) are found immersed in an external electric field gradient.

Quaestiones quaedam philosophicae (Certain philosophical questions) is the name given to a set of notes that [Isaac Newton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isaac_Newton) kept for himself during his earlier years in Cambridge.

Quanta is an [open access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_access) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering the [foundations of quantum mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_foundations), [mathematical physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_physics), and [philosophy of science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philosophy_of_science).
Quantinuum is a [quantum computing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_computing) company formed by the merger of Cambridge Quantum and Honeywell Quantum Solutions.

term: Quantities, Units and Symbols in Physical Chemistry
page: Quantities, Units and Symbols in Physical Chemistry
definition: Quantities, Units and Symbols in Physical Chemistry, also known as the Green Book, is a compilation of terms and symbols widely used in the field of [physical chemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physical_chemistry).
categories: International Union of Pure and Applied Physics
related: International Union of Pure and Applied Physics

definition: Quantization (in British English quantisation) is the systematic transition procedure from a classical understanding of physical phenomena to a newer understanding known as [quantum mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics).
quantum or quantized enveloping algebra is a [q-analog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Q-analog) of a [universal enveloping algebra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_enveloping_algebra).

media.file: Brand logo of Quantum - the open journal for quantum science.png

definition: quantum (: quanta) is the minimum amount of any physical entity ([physical property](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physical_property)) involved in an [interaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fundamental_interaction).
Quantum 1/f noise is an intrinsic and fundamental part of [quantum mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics).
quantum acoustics is the study of [sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sound) under conditions such that [quantum mechanical effects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics) are relevant.

quantum affine algebra (or affine quantum group) is a [Hopf algebra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hopf_algebra) that is a q-deformation of the [universal enveloping algebra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_enveloping_algebra) of an [affine Lie algebra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Affine_Lie_algebra).

quantum algorithm is an [algorithm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algorithm) that runs on a realistic model of [quantum computation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_computation), the most commonly used model being the [quantum circuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_circuit) model of computation.

quantum amplifier is an [amplifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amplifier) that uses [quantum mechanical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics) methods to amplify a signal; examples include the active elements of [laser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laser)s and [optical amplifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_amplifier)s.

Quantum annealing (QA) is an optimization process for finding the [global minimum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_minimum) of a given [objective function](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Objective_function) over a given set of candidate solutions (candidate states), by a process using [quantum fluctuation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_fluctuation)s.

Quantum Artificial Intelligence Lab (also called the Quantum AI Lab or QuAIL) is a joint initiative of [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA), [Universities Space Research Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universities_Space_Research_Association), and [Google](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google) (specifically, Google Research) whose goal is to pioneer research on how [quantum computing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_computing) might help with [machine learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_learning) and other difficult computer science problems.

quantum battery is a type of [electric battery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_battery) that uses the principles of [quantum mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics) to store energy.

quantum beats are simple examples of [phenomena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenomena) that cannot be described by semiclassical theory, but can be described by fully quantized calculation, especially [quantum electrodynamics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_electrodynamics).

Quantum biology is the study of applications of [quantum mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics) and [theoretical chemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theoretical_chemistry) to aspects of [biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biology) that cannot be accurately described by the classical laws of physics.

quantum boomerang effect is a [quantum mechanical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics) phenomenon whereby [wavepackets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wave_packet) launched through [disordered](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randomness) media return, on average, to their starting points, as a consequence of [Anderson localization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anderson_localization) and the inherent symmetries of the system.

quantum bus is a device which can be used to store or transfer information between independent [qubits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qubits) in a [quantum computer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_computer), or combine two qubits into a [superposition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superposition_principle).

quantum capacity is the highest rate at which [quantum information](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_information) can be communicated over many independent uses of a noisy [quantum channel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_channel) from a sender to a receiver.

quantum catalyst is a special [ancillary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancilla_bit) [quantum state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_state) whose presence enables certain local [transformations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformation_(function)) that would otherwise be impossible.

quantum cellular automaton (QCA) is an abstract model of [quantum computation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_computation), devised in analogy to conventional models of [cellular automata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cellular_automata) introduced by [John von Neumann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_von_Neumann).
quantum channel is a communication channel that can transmit [quantum information](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_information), as well as classical information.

Quantum chaos is a branch of [physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physics) focused on how [chaotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaos_theory) classical [dynamical systems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dynamical_systems) can be described in terms of quantum theory.
quantum Cheshire cat is a quantum phenomenom that suggests that a particle's physical properties can take a different trajectory from that of the particle itself.

quantum chromodynamics (QCD) is the study of the [strong interaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strong_interaction) between [quark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quark)s mediated by [gluon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gluon)s.

Quantum chromodynamics binding energy (QCD binding energy), gluon binding energy or chromodynamic binding energy is the [energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy) binding [quark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quark)s together into [hadron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hadron)s.
Quantum circuit cutting is a method to partition a large [quantum circuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_circuit) into smaller, more manageable parts.
quantum clock model is a quantum lattice model.
Quantum cloning is a process that takes an arbitrary, unknown [quantum state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_state) and makes an exact copy without altering the original state in any way.
Quantum complex networks are [complex networks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex_network) whose nodes are [quantum computing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_computing) devices.

Quantum complexity theory is the subfield of [computational complexity theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computational_complexity_theory) that deals with [complexity classes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complexity_classes) defined using [quantum computers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_computers), a [computational model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computational_model) based on [quantum mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics).

Quantum Computation Language (QCL) is one of the first implemented [quantum programming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_programming) [languages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Programming_languages).

media.file: IBM Quantum Computer Demo at ITUWTSA 2024, Delhi 2.jpg

definition: Quantum computing scaling laws (sometimes abbreviated as QC scaling laws) are a set of observations describing the [exponential growth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exponential_growth) of various aspects of [quantum computer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_computing) development.

Quantum contextuality is a feature of the [phenomenology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenomenology_(physics)) of [quantum mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics) whereby measurements of quantum [observable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Observable)s cannot simply be thought of as revealing pre-existing values.
quantum correlation is the [expected value](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expected_value) of the product of the alternative outcomes.
Quantum counting algorithm is a [quantum algorithm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_algorithm) for efficiently counting the number of solutions for a given search problem.
quantum Cramér–Rao bound is the quantum analogue of the classical [Cramér–Rao bound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cramér–Rao_bound).

quantum critical point is a point in the [phase diagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phase_diagram) of a material where a continuous [phase transition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phase_transition) takes place at [absolute zero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_zero).

Quantum crystallography is a branch of [crystallography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crystallography) that investigates crystalline materials within the framework of [quantum mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics), with analysis and representation, in [position](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Position_space) or in [momentum space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Momentum_space), of quantities like [wave function](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wave_function), [electron charge and spin density](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron_density), [density matrices](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Density_matrices) and all properties related to them (like [electric potential](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_potential), electric or magnetic moments, energy densities, [electron localization function](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron_localization_function), one electron potential, etc.).

Quantum Darwinism is a theory meant to explain the emergence of the [classical world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classical_physics) from the [quantum world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics) as due to a process of [Darwinian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Darwin) [natural selection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_selection) induced by the environment interacting with the quantum system; where the many possible [quantum states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_states) are selected against in favor of a stable [pointer state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pointer_state).
Quantum decoherence is the loss of [[Coherence (physics)#Quantum coherence|quantum coherence]].
quantum defect refers to the shift in frequency between the [pump beam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pump_beam) and the output radiation.
quantum depolarizing channel is a model for [quantum noise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_noise) in quantum systems.

Quantum Digital Signature (QDS) refers to the quantum mechanical equivalent of either a classical [digital signature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_signature) or, more generally, a handwritten signature on a paper document.

quantum dimer magnet state is one in which [quantum spins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin_(physics)) in a [magnetic structure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnetic_structure) entangle to form a [singlet state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singlet_state).

Quantum [dimer model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dimer_model)s were introduced to model the physics of [resonating valence bond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resonating_valence_bond) (RVB) states in [lattice spin systems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lattice_spin_systems).
quantum discord is a measure of nonclassical correlations between two subsystems of a [quantum system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_system).
Quantum dissipation is the branch of [physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physics) that studies the quantum analogues of the process of irreversible loss of energy observed at the classical level.

Quantum dots (QDs) or semiconductor nanocrystals are [semiconductor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semiconductor) particles a few [nanometre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanometre)s in size with [optical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Light) and [electronic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronics) properties that differ from those of larger particles via [quantum mechanical effects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics).

Quantum dot cellular automata (QDCA, sometimes referred to simply as [quantum cellular automata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_cellular_automaton), or QCA) are a proposed improvement on conventional computer design ([CMOS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CMOS)), which have been devised in analogy to conventional models of [cellular automata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cellular_automata) introduced by [John von Neumann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_von_Neumann).

quantum dot display is a [display device](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Display_device) that uses [quantum dots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_dots) (QDs), semiconductor nanocrystals which can produce pure monochromatic red, green, and blue light.

quantum dot laser is a [semiconductor laser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semiconductor_laser) that uses [quantum dot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_dot)s as the [active medium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Active_medium) for stimulated emission of light.
quantum dot single-photon source is based on a single [quantum dot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_dot) placed in an [optical cavity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_cavity).

quantum dot solar cell (QDSC) is a [solar cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_cell) design that uses [quantum dot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_dot)s as the captivating photovoltaic material.

media.file: Sargent Group quantum dot solar cell.jpg

definition: quantum double model, proposed by [Alexei Kitaev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexei_Kitaev), is a lattice model that exhibits topological excitations.
quantum efficiency (QE) of a [photodetector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photodetector) is a measure of its electrical response to light.
Quantum Electronics is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal).
Quantum energy teleportation (QET) is an application of [quantum information science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_information_science).
Quantum engineering is the development of technology that capitalizes on the laws of quantum mechanics.

Quantum entanglement is the phenomenon in which the [quantum state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_state) of each [particle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subatomic_particle) in a group cannot be described independently of the state of the others, even when the particles are separated by a large distance.

quantum eraser experiment is an [interferometer experiment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interferometer) that demonstrates several fundamental aspects of [quantum mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics), including [quantum entanglement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_entanglement) and [complementarity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complementarity_(physics)).

quantum ergodicity is a property of the [quantization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantization_(physics)) of [classical mechanical systems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classical_mechanics) that are [chaotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaos_theory) in the sense of exponential sensitivity to initial conditions.
Quantum Experiment using Satellite Technology was launched in 2017 by the [Raman Research Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raman_Research_Institute).

Quantum feedback or quantum feedback control is a class of methods to prepare and manipulate a quantum system in which that system's [quantum state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_state) or trajectory is used to evolve the system towards some desired outcome.

quantum field theory (QFT) is a theoretical framework that combines [field theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Field_theory_(physics)), [special relativity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_relativity) and [quantum mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics).

term: Quantum Field Theory in a Nutshell
page: Quantum Field Theory in a Nutshell

term: Quantum field theory in curved spacetime
page: Quantum field theory in curved spacetime
definition: quantum field theory in curved spacetime (QFTCS) Gravity is not [renormalizable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renormalizable) in QFT, so merely formulating QFT in curved spacetime is not a true theory of quantum gravity.

Quantum finance is an interdisciplinary research field that applies theories and methods developed by [quantum physicists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics) and [economists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economics) to [finance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finance).

Quantum fingerprinting is a proposed technique that uses a [quantum computer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_computer) to generate a string with a similar function to the [cryptographic hash function](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryptographic_hash_function).

quantum finite automata (QFA) or quantum state machines are a quantum analog of [probabilistic automata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Probabilistic_automata) or a [Markov decision process](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Markov_decision_process).

quantum Fisher information is a central quantity in [quantum metrology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_metrology) and is the quantum analogue of the classical [Fisher information](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fisher_information).
Quantum Technologies Flagship is a [European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union) scientific research initiative.

quantum fluid refers to any system that exhibits quantum mechanical effects at the macroscopic level such as [superfluid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superfluid)s, [superconductor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superconductor)s, [ultracold atoms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultracold_atoms), etc.

Quantum Flux Parametron (QFP) is a [digital logic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_logic) implementation technology based on [superconducting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superconductivity) [Josephson junction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josephson_junction)s.

Quantum foam (also known as spacetime foam, or spacetime bubble) is a theoretical [quantum fluctuation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_fluctuation) of [spacetime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spacetime) on very small scales due to [quantum mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics).

Quantum foundations is a [discipline of science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discipline_(academia)) and [philosophy of physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philosophy_of_physics) that seeks to understand the most counter-intuitive aspects of [quantum theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics), reformulate it and even propose new [generalization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generalization)s thereof.

quantum Fourier transform (QFT) is a [linear transformation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linear_transformation) on [quantum bits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qubit), and is the quantum analogue of the [discrete Fourier transform](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discrete_Fourier_transform).
Quantum game theory is an extension of classical [game theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_theory) to the quantum domain.

quantum geometry is the set of mathematical concepts that generalize [geometry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geometry) to describe physical phenomena at distance scales comparable to the [Planck length](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planck_length).

Quantum geometry in condensed matter physics refers to gauge-invariant geometric properties of quantum states as functions of external parameters—most commonly the crystal momentum of [Bloch-band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloch_wave) eigenstates in a periodic solid.

quantum graph is a linear, network-shaped structure of vertices connected on edges (i.e., a [graph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graph_(discrete_mathematics))) in which each edge is given a length and where a differential (or pseudo-differential) equation is posed on each edge.

Quantum gravity (QG) is a field of [theoretical physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theoretical_physics) that seeks [unification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unification_of_theories_in_physics) of the theory of [gravity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gravity) with the principles of [quantum mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics).
quantum group denotes one of a few different kinds of [noncommutative algebra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noncommutative_algebra)s with additional structure.

quantum [gyroscope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gyroscope) is a very sensitive device to measure [angular rotation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angular_momentum) based on [quantum mechanical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics) principles.

quantum Hall effect (or integer quantum Hall effect) is a [quantized](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics) version of the [Hall effect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hall_effect) which is observed in [two-dimensional electron systems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2DEG) subjected to low [temperature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temperature)s and strong [magnetic field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnetic_field)s, in which the Hall [resistance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrical_resistance_and_conductance) {{math|R 617–647 (1986).

quantum harmonic oscillator is the [quantum-mechanical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics) analog of the [classical harmonic oscillator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harmonic_oscillator).

quantum Heisenberg model, developed by [Werner Heisenberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Werner_Heisenberg), is a [statistical mechanical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statistical_mechanics) [model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_model) used in the study of [critical point](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Critical_point_(thermodynamics))s and [phase transition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phase_transition)s of magnetic systems, in which the [spin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin_(physics))s of the magnetic systems are treated [quantum mechanically](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics).

Quantum illumination is a paradigm for target detection that employs [quantum entanglement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_entanglement) between a signal electromagnetic mode and an idler electromagnetic mode, as well as joint measurement of these modes.

Quantum image processing (QIMP) is using [quantum computing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_computing) or [quantum information processing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_information_processing) to create and work with [quantum image](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_image)s.

Quantum indeterminacy is the apparent necessary incompleteness in the description of a [physical system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physical_system), that has become one of the characteristics of the standard description of [quantum physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_physics).

Quantum information is the [information](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Information) of the [state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_state) of a [quantum system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_system).

Quantum information science is an interdisciplinary field that combines the principles of [quantum mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics), [information theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Information_theory), and [computer science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_science) to explore how quantum phenomena can be harnessed for the processing, analysis, and transmission of information.

quantum instrument is a mathematical description of a quantum measurement, capturing both the [classical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classical_physics) and [quantum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_physics) outputs.

quantum inverse scattering method, similar to the closely related algebraic Bethe ansatz, is a method for solving [integrable model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Integrable_system)s in 1+1 dimensions, introduced by [Leon Takhtajan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leon_Takhtajan) and [[Ludvig Faddeev|L.

quantum jump is the abrupt [transition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_electron_transition) of a quantum system ([atom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atom), [molecule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecule), [atomic nucleus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_nucleus)) from one [quantum state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_state) to another, from one [energy level](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy_level) to another.

quantum jump method, also known as the [Monte Carlo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monte_Carlo_method) wave function (MCWF) is a technique in [computational physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computational_physics) used for simulating [open quantum system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_quantum_system)s and [quantum dissipation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_dissipation).

Quantum key distribution (QKD) is a [secure communication](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secure_communication) method that implements a [cryptographic protocol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryptographic_protocol) based on the laws of [quantum mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics), specifically quantum entanglement, the measurement-disturbance principle, and the no-cloning theorem.

quantum KZ equations or quantum Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov equations or qKZ equations are the analogue for [quantum affine algebra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_affine_algebra)s of the [Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov equations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov_equations) for [affine Kac–Moody algebras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kac–Moody_algebra).

LC circuit is a variety of resonant circuit, and consists of an [inductor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inductor), represented by the letter L, and a [capacitor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capacitor), represented by the letter C.
quantum limit in physics is a limit on measurement accuracy at quantum scales.

Quantum lithography is a type of [photolithography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photolithography), which exploits non-classical properties of the photons, such as [quantum entanglement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_entanglement), in order to achieve superior performance over ordinary classical lithography.

quantum clock is a type of [atomic clock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_clock) with [laser cooled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laser_cooled) single [ion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ion)s confined together in an [electromagnetic ion trap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ion_trap).
quantum logic gate (or simply quantum gate) is a basic quantum circuit operating on a small number of [qubit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qubit)s.
quantum machine is a human-made device whose collective motion follows the laws of [quantum mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics).
Quantum machine learning (QML) is the study of [quantum algorithms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_algorithms) for [machine learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_learning).
quantum Markov semigroup describes the dynamics in a [Markovian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Markov_Property) [open quantum system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_quantum_system).

Quantum materials is an umbrella term in [condensed matter physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Condensed_matter_physics) that encompasses all materials whose essential properties cannot be described in terms of [semiclassical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semiclassical_physics) particles and low-level [quantum mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics).

term: Quantum mechanical scattering of photon and nucleus
page: Quantum mechanical scattering of photon and nucleus

definition: quantum memory is the [quantum-mechanical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics) version of ordinary [computer memory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_memory).
quantum metrological gain is defined in the context of carrying out a metrological task using a [quantum state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_state) of a multiparticle system.

Quantum metrology is the study of making high-resolution and highly sensitive measurements of physical parameters using quantum theory to describe the physical systems, == See also == * [Quantum metrological gain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_metrological_gain) * [Dimensional metrology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dimensional_metrology) * [Forensic metrology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forensic_metrology) * [Smart Metrology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smart_Metrology) * [Time metrology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_metrology) == References == [[Category:Quantum information science]] [[Category:Quantum

quantum mind or quantum consciousness is a group of hypotheses proposing that local physical laws and interactions from [classical mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classical_mechanics) or connections between neurons alone cannot explain [consciousness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consciousness).
quantum mirage is a peculiar result in [quantum chaos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_chaos).

quantum money scheme is a [quantum cryptographic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_Cryptography) protocol that creates and verifies banknotes that are resistant to [forge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forgery)ry.
Quantum Monte Carlo encompasses a large family of computational methods whose common aim is the study of complex [quantum system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_system)s.

quantum mutual information (QMI), or von Neumann mutual information, after [John von Neumann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_von_Neumann), is a measure of correlation between subsystems of [quantum state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_state).

Quantum natural language processing (QNLP) is the application of [quantum computing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_computing) to [natural language processing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_language_processing) (NLP).

Quantum neural networks are [computational neural network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_network_(machine_learning)) models which are based on the principles of [quantum mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics).

definition: Quantum noise is any [noise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noise_(spectral_phenomenon)) arising from quantum mechanical phenomena such as [field quantization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_quantization) or [the uncertainty principle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uncertainty_principle).

Quantum non-equilibrium is a concept within stochastic formulations of the [De Broglie–Bohm theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Broglie–Bohm_theory) of [quantum physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics).

Quantum nondemolition (QND) measurement is a special type of [measurement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Measurement_in_quantum_mechanics) of a [quantum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics) system in which the uncertainty of the measured [observable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Observable) does not increase from its measured value during the subsequent normal evolution of the system.

quantum nonlocality refers to the phenomenon by which the [measurement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Measurement_in_quantum_mechanics) statistics of a multipartite [quantum system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_system) do not allow an interpretation with [local hidden variables](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_hidden_variables).
quantum numbers are quantities that characterize the possible states of the system.

quantum operation (also known as quantum dynamical map or [quantum process](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_process)) is a mathematical formalism used to describe a broad class of transformations that a quantum mechanical system can undergo.

Quantum optics is a branch of [atomic, molecular, and optical physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic,_molecular,_and_optical_physics) and [quantum chemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_chemistry) that studies the behavior of [photon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photon)s (individual quanta of light).
Quantum optimization algorithms are [quantum algorithms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_algorithms) that are used to solve optimization problems.

quantum oscillations describes a series of related [experimental](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Experimental_physics) techniques used to map the [Fermi surface](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fermi_surface) of a [metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metal) in the presence of a strong [magnetic field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnetic_field).
quantum pendulum is a theoretical model and experimental system that studies how a pendulum behaves under [quantum mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics).

quantum phase estimation algorithm is a [quantum algorithm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_algorithm) to estimate the phase corresponding to an eigenvalue of a given [unitary operator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unitary_matrix).

quantum phase transition (QPT) is a [phase transition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phase_transition) between different [quantum phases](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_phases) ([phases of matter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phase_(matter)) at [zero temperature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_zero)).
Quantum phases are quantum states of matter at zero temperature.

quantum potential or quantum potentiality is a central concept of the [de Broglie–Bohm formulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Broglie–Bohm_theory) of [quantum mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics), introduced by [David Bohm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Bohm) in 1952.
quantum process is a somewhat ambiguous term which usually refers to the time evolution of an ([open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_quantum_system)) quantum system.

Quantum programming refers to the process of designing and implementing algorithms that operate on [quantum systems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_computing), typically using quantum circuits composed of quantum gates, measurements, and classical control logic.
Quantum pseudo-telepathy describes the use of [quantum entanglement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_entanglement) to eliminate the need for classical communications.

Quantum radar is a [remote-sensing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Remote_sensing) technology based on quantum-mechanical effects, such as the [uncertainty principle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uncertainty_principle) or [quantum entanglement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_entanglement).

Quantum random access codes (QRACs) are a quantum information theoretic primitive used to encode a string of classical bits into a quantum state of smaller dimension, such that any single bit of the original string can be retrieved with a certain probability of success.

Quantum random circuits (QRC) is a concept of incorporating an element of randomness into the local [unitary operations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unitarity_(physics)) and [measurements](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Measurement_in_quantum_mechanics) of a [quantum circuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_circuit).
Quantum readout is a method to verify the authenticity of an object.

Quantum refereed game in quantum information processing is a class of [games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_theory) in the [general theory of quantum games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_game_theory).
quantum reference frame is a [reference frame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reference_frame) which is treated [quantum theoretically](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics).

Quantum reflection is a uniquely quantum phenomenon in which an object, such as a neutron or a small molecule, reflects smoothly and in a wavelike fashion from a much larger surface, such as a pool of mercury.
quantum register is a system comprising multiple [qubits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qubit).

Quantum regression theorem (QRT) is a result in [quantum statistical mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_statistical_mechanics) and [quantum optics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_optics) that provides a rule for computing multi-time [correlation functions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Correlation_function_(statistical_mechanics)) from the same [reduced dynamics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reduced_dynamics) that describes one-time [expectation values](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expectation_value_(quantum_mechanics)) of an [open quantum system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_quantum_system).
quantum relative entropy is a measure of distinguishability between two [quantum states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Density_matrix).
quantum revival is a periodic recurrence of the quantum [wave function](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wave_function) during its time-evolution.

Quantum secret sharing (QSS) is a [quantum cryptographic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_cryptography) scheme for [secure communication](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secure_communication) that extends beyond simple [quantum key distribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_key_distribution).
Quantum singular value transformation is a framework for designing [quantum algorithm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_algorithm)s.

Quantum social science is an emerging field of interdisciplinary research that draws parallels between [quantum physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics) and the [social science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_science)s.

quantum solvent is essentially a [superfluid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superfluid) (aka a [quantum liquid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_hydrodynamics)) used to [dissolve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solvation) another [chemical species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_species).
quantum sort is any [sorting algorithm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sorting_algorithm) that runs on a [quantum computer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_computer).

quantum spacetime is a generalization of the usual concept of [spacetime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spacetime) in which some variables that ordinarily [commute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commutative_property) are assumed not to commute and form a different [Lie algebra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lie_algebra).
quantum speed limit (QSL) is a limitation on the minimum time for a quantum system to evolve between two distinguishable (orthogonal) states.

quantum spin Hall state is a [state of matter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_of_matter) in two-dimensional [semiconductors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semiconductor) that have a quantized spin-Hall conductance and a vanishing charge-Hall conductance.

quantum spin liquid is a [phase of matter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/States_of_matter) that can be formed by interacting [quantum spins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin_(physics)) in certain magnetic materials.

Quantum spin tunneling, or quantum tunneling of magnetization, is a physical phenomenon by which the quantum mechanical state that describes the collective magnetization of a [nanomagnet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanomagnet) is a linear superposition of two states with well defined and opposite magnetization.
quantum state is a mathematical entity that represents a physical system.

quantum state discrimination collectively refers to quantum-informatics techniques, with the help of which, by performing a small number of measurements on a physical system, its specific quantum state can be identified .

quantum state purification refers to the process of representing a [mixed state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixed_state_(physics)) as a [pure quantum state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pure_state) of higher-dimensional [Hilbert space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilbert_space).
quantum state space is an abstract [space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space) in which different Sons.
Quantum statistical mechanics is [statistical mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statistical_mechanics) applied to [quantum mechanical systems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics).

quantum steering is a special kind of nonlocal correlation, which is intermediate between [Bell nonlocality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bell's_theorem) and [quantum entanglement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_entanglement).
pump is an [alternating current](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alternating_current)-driven device that generates a [direct current](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Direct_current) (DC).

Quantum stochastic calculus is a generalization of [stochastic calculus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stochastic_calculus) to [noncommuting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commutative_property) variables.

Quantum suicide is a [thought experiment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thought_experiment) in [quantum mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics) and the [philosophy of physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philosophy_of_physics).

Quantum superposition is a fundamental principle of [quantum mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics) that states that [linear combination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linear_combination)s of [solutions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solution_(mathematics)) to the [Schrödinger equation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schrödinger_equation) are also solutions of the Schrödinger equation.

definition: quantum supremacy or quantum advantage is the goal of demonstrating that a [programmable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_programming) quantum computer can solve a problem that no [classical computer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classical_computer) can solve in any feasible amount of time, irrespective of the usefulness of the problem.

quantum t-design is a [probability distribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Probability_distribution) over either pure [quantum states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_states) or unitary operators which can duplicate properties of the probability distribution over the [Haar measure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haar_measure) for polynomials of degree t or less.
Quantum teleportation is a technique for transferring [quantum information](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_information) from a sender at one location to a receiver some distance away.

categories: Philosophy of thermal and statistical physics

definition: Quantum tic-tac-toe is a no more spooky marks may be placed in it.

Quantum [tomography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomography) or quantum state tomography is the process by which a quantum state is reconstructed using measurements on an ensemble of identical quantum states.

Quantum topology is a branch of mathematics that connects [quantum mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics) with [low-dimensional topology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Low-dimensional_topology).

Quantum Trajectory Theory (QTT) is a formulation of [quantum mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics) used for simulating [open quantum system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_quantum_system)s, [quantum dissipation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_dissipation) and single quantum systems.
Quantum triviality is referred to a possible situation in quantum field theories, when the effective charge tends to zero in the limit of large length scales.

quantum tunnelling, barrier penetration, or simply tunnelling is a [quantum mechanical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics) phenomenon in which an object such as an electron or atom passes through a [potential energy barrier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potential_barrier) that, according to [classical mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classical_mechanics), should not be passable due to the object not having sufficient energy to pass or surmount the barrier.

Quantum tunnelling composites (QTCs) are [composite material](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Composite_material)s of [metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metal)s and non-[conducting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrical_conductance) [elastomer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elastomer)ic binder, used as [pressure sensor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pressure_sensor)s.

quantum vacuum state (also called the quantum vacuum or vacuum state) is the [quantum state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_state) with the lowest possible [energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy).
Quantum volume is a metric that measures the capabilities and error rates of a [quantum computer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_computing).
Quantum walks are [quantum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics) analogs of classical [random walks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Random_walk).

quantum walk search (sometimes regarded as QFS, similar to [DFS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depth-first_search) and [BFS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breadth-first_search)) is a [quantum algorithm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_algorithm) for finding a marked node in a graph.

quantum-confined [Stark effect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stark_effect) (QCSE) describes the effect of an external [electric field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_field) upon the light [absorption spectrum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absorption_spectrum) or [emission spectrum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emission_spectrum) of a [quantum well](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_well) (QW).

Quasi-crystals are [supramolecular aggregates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supramolecular_chemistry) exhibiting both [crystalline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crystalline) (solid) properties as well as amorphous, [liquid-like](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liquid_crystal) properties.

quasi-harmonic approximation is a [phonon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phonon)-based model of [solid-state physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solid-state_physics) used to describe volume-dependent thermal effects, such as the [thermal expansion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thermal_expansion).

quasi-isodynamic (QI) stellarator is a type of [stellarator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stellarator) (a [magnetic confinement fusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnetic_confinement_fusion) reactor) that satisfies the property of [omnigeneity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omnigeneity), avoids the potentially hazardous toroidal [bootstrap current](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bootstrap_current), and has minimal [neoclassical transport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neoclassical_transport) in the collisionless regime.

Quasi-phase-matching is a technique in [nonlinear optics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nonlinear_optics) which allows a positive net flow of energy from the pump frequency to the signal and idler frequencies by creating a periodic structure in the nonlinear medium.
Quasi-set theory is a formal mathematical theory for dealing with collections of objects, some of which may be indistinguishable from one another.

Quasioptics concerns the propagation of [electromagnetic radiation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electromagnetic_radiation) where the [wavelength](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wavelength) is comparable to the size of the optical components (e.g.
quasiparticle is a concept used to describe a collective behavior of a group of particles that can be treated as if they were a single particle.

Quasiparticle interference (QPI) imaging is a technique used in [condensed matter physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Condensed_matter_physics) that allows a [scanning tunneling microscope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scanning_tunneling_microscope) to image the electronic structure of a material and infer information about the momentum space electronic structure from imaging the density of states in real space.

quasiprobability distribution is a [mathematical object](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_object) similar to a [probability distribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Probability_distribution) but which relaxes some of [Kolmogorov's axioms of probability theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Probability_axioms).

reflection coefficient is a parameter that describes how much of a wave is reflected by an impedance discontinuity in the transmission medium.

refraction is the redirection of a [wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wave) as it passes from one [medium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transmission_medium) to another.

Refractive index contrast, in an [optical waveguide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_waveguide), such as an [optical fiber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_fiber), is a measure of the relative difference in [refractive index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Refractive_index) of the [[Fiber optics#Principle of operation|core]] and [cladding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cladding_(fiber_optics)).

regularization is a method of modifying [observables](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Observables) which have [singularities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singularity_(mathematics)) in order to make them finite by the introduction of a suitable parameter called the regulator.

single-layer materials or 2D materials refers to [crystal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crystal)line solids consisting of a single layer of atoms.

Skin friction drag or viscous drag is a type of [aerodynamic or hydrodynamic drag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drag_(physics)), which is resistant force exerted on an object moving in a fluid.

Slater determinant is an expression that describes the [wave function](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wave_function) of a multi-[fermion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fermion)ic system.
Slater integrals are certain integrals of products of three [spherical harmonic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spherical_harmonic)s.

Slater-type orbitals (STOs) or Slater-type functions (STFs) are functions used as [atomic orbital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_orbital)s in the [linear combination of atomic orbitals molecular orbital method](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linear_combination_of_atomic_orbitals_molecular_orbital_method).

soft SUSY breaking is type of [supersymmetry breaking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supersymmetry_breaking) that does not cause [ultraviolet divergence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultraviolet_divergence)s to appear in scalar masses.

softening point is the temperature at which a material softens beyond some arbitrary softness.

Soil physics is the study of [soil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soil)'s physical properties and processes.

thermal properties of soil are a component of [soil physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soil_physics) that has found important uses in [engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Engineering), [climatology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climatology) and [agriculture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agriculture).
Sokolov–Ternov effect is the effect of self-polarization of relativistic electrons or positrons moving at high energy in a [magnetic field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnetic_field).

Solar gain (also known as solar heat gain or passive solar gain) is the increase in thermal energy of a space, object or structure as it absorbs incident [solar radiation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_energy).

Solar phenomena are [natural phenomena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_phenomena) which occur within the [atmosphere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stellar_atmosphere) of the [Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun).

Solar radio emission refers to [radio wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio_wave)s that are naturally produced by the [Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun), primarily from the lower and upper layers of the atmosphere called the [chromosphere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromosphere) and [corona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stellar_corona), respectively.

Solarsoft is a collaborative software development system created at [Lockheed-Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lockheed-Martin) to support solar data analysis and [spacecraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spacecraft) operation activities.

Solar–hydrogen energy cycle is an energy cycle where a [solar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_energy) powered [electrolyzer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrolyzer) is used to convert water to [hydrogen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrogen) and [oxygen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxygen).

soliton is used to refer to any [optical field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_field) that does not change during propagation because of a delicate balance between [nonlinear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nonlinearity) and [dispersive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dispersion_(optics)) effects in the medium.

definition: Spin is an [intrinsic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intrinsic_and_extrinsic_properties) form of [angular momentum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angular_momentum) carried by [elementary particle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elementary_particle)s, and thus by [[List of particles#Composite particles|composite particles]] such as [hadron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hadron)s, [atomic nuclei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_nucleus), and atoms.
spin contamination is the artificial mixing of different [electron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron)ic [spin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin_(physics))-states.
Spin-density wave (SDW) and [charge-density wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charge-density_wave) (CDW) are names for two similar low-energy ordered states of solids.
Spin diffusion describes a situation wherein the individual nuclear [spins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin_(physics)) undergo continuous exchange of energy.

spin echo or Hahn echo is the refocusing of [spin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin_(physics)) magnetisation by a pulse of resonant [electromagnetic radiation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electromagnetic_radiation).
Spin engineering describes the control and manipulation of [quantum spin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_spin) systems to develop devices and materials.

definition: Spin gapless semiconductors are a class of materials in which the spin-averaged [electronic band structure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_band_structure) has no [band gap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Band_gap), while the two spin channels are asymmetrical.
spin Hall effect (SHE) is a transport phenomenon predicted by Russian physicists [[Mikhail Dyakonov|Mikhail I.

spin Nernst effect is a phenomenon of spin current generation caused by the thermal flow of [electron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron)s or [magnons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnon) in condensed matter.

spin network is a type of diagram which can be used to represent [states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_state) and interactions between [particles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Particle_physics) and [fields](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_field_theory) in [quantum mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics).

spin probe is a [molecule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecule) with stable [free radical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_radical) character that carries a [functional group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Functional_group).

spin quantum number is a [quantum number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_number) (designated ) that describes the intrinsic [angular momentum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angular_momentum) (or spin angular momentum, or simply [spin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin_(physics))) of an [electron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron) or other [particle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elementary_particle).

spin qubit quantum computer is a [quantum computer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_computer) based on controlling the [spin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin_(physics)) of [charge carrier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charge_carrier)s ([electron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron)s and [electron hole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron_hole)s) in [semiconductor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semiconductor) devices.

Spin squeezing is a quantum process that decreases the variance of one of the angular momentum quadratures below the standard [quantum limit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_limit), at the expense of increasing variance in another, in an ensemble of particles with spin.

spin stiffness or spin rigidity is a constant which represents the change in the [ground state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ground_state) energy of a spin system as a result of introducing a slow in-plane twist of the spins.
spin tensor is a quantity used to describe the [rotational motion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotational_motion) of particles in [spacetime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spacetime).

spin transition is an example of transition between two [electronic state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_state)s in [molecular chemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_chemistry), which have nearly identical energy levels.

spin valve is a device, consisting of two or more conducting magnetic materials, whose [electrical resistance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrical_resistance) can change between two values depending on the relative alignment of the magnetization in the layers.
spin-destruction (or spin-disorientation) collision is a physical impact where the spin angular momentum of an atom is irretrievably scrambled.
spin-exchange is an interaction process between two particles mediated by an [exchange interaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exchange_interaction).

Spinodal decomposition is a mechanism by which a single thermodynamic [phase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phase_(matter)) spontaneously separates into two phases (without [nucleation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleation)).

Spinons are one of three [quasiparticle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quasiparticle)s, along with [holon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holon_(physics))s and [orbiton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orbiton)s, that [electron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron)s in solids are able to split into during the process of [spin–charge separation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin–charge_separation), when extremely tightly confined at temperatures close to [absolute zero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_zero).

spin–orbit interaction (also called spin–orbit effect or spin–orbit coupling) is a [relativistic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_relativity) interaction of a particle's [spin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin_(physics)) with its motion inside a [potential](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potential_well).

Spitzer resistivity (or plasma resistivity), also called 'Spitzer-Harm resistivity', is an expression describing the [electrical resistance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrical_resistance_and_conductance) in a [plasma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plasma_(physics)), which was first formulated by [Lyman Spitzer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyman_Spitzer) in 1950.
splice box (also known as splice distributor) is a housing in which fiber optic cables begin or end.
split supersymmetry is a proposal for physics [beyond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physics_beyond_the_Standard_Model) the [Standard Model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_Model).

Spontaneous parametric down-conversion (also known as SPDC, parametric fluorescence or parametric scattering) is a nonlinear instant optical process that converts one photon of higher energy (namely, a pump photon) into a pair of photons (namely, signal and idler photons) of lower energy, in accordance with the laws of [energy conservation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_of_conservation_of_energy) and [momentum conservation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_of_conservation_of_momentum).

definition: top quark condensate theory (or top condensation) is an alternative to the [Standard Model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_Model) fundamental [Higgs field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Higgs_field), where the Higgs boson is a [composite field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Composite_field), composed of the [top quark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Top_quark) and its [antiquark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antiquark).
top-down cosmology is a proposal to regard the many possible histories of a given event as having real existence.

Topcolor is a model in [theoretical physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theoretical_physics), of dynamical [electroweak symmetry breaking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electroweak_symmetry_breaking) in which the [top quark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Top_quark) and anti-top quark [form a composite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Top_quark_condensate) [Higgs boson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Higgs_boson) by a new force arising from massive [[Category:Physics beyond the Standard Model]] acun7kx3dm7r7wbign0snelcwbxmkiv

topological degeneracy is a phenomenon in which the [ground state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ground_state) of a [gapped many-body Hamiltonian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gapped_Hamiltonian) becomes degenerate in the [limit of large system size](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thermodynamic_limit) such that the degeneracy cannot be lifted by any [local perturbation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_perturbation)s.

topological entanglement entropy spin-liquid, [quantum dimer models](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_dimer_models) on non-bipartite lattices, and Kitaev's [toric code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toric_code) state, are characterized γ = log(2).

topological quantum field theory (or topological field theory or TQFT) is a [quantum field theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_field_theory) that computes [topological invariant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Topological_invariant)s.

topological quantum number (also called topological charge) is any quantity, in a physical theory, that takes on only one of a discrete set of values, due to [topological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Topology) considerations.
topological recursion is a recursive definition of invariants of spectral curves.

topological star (also called a topological soliton in this context) is a smooth, [horizonless](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horizon_(general_relativity)) solution of the five-dimensional [Einstein–Maxwell equations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Einstein–Maxwell_equations) whose interior contains [non-trivial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-trivial) [topological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Topological) cycles threaded by [magnetic flux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnetic_flux).
topological string theory is a version of [string theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/String_theory).

topological superconductor is a material that [conducts electricity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_current) with zero [electrical resistivity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrical_resistivity_and_conductivity), and has non-trivial topology which gives it certain unique properties.

definition: toroidal moment is an independent term in the [multipole expansion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multipole_expansion) of the [electromagnetic field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electromagnetic_field) which is distinct from magnetic and electric [multipole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multipole)s.

[toroidal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toroid_(geometry)) ring model, known originally as the Parson magneton or magnetic electron, is a physical model of [subatomic particle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subatomic_particle)s.

Torricelli's experiment was invented in [Pisa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pisa) in 1643 by the Italian scientist [Evangelista Torricelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evangelista_Torricelli) (1608-1647).

torsion is the twisting of an object due to an applied [torque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torque).

Torsional instability is a mechanical phenomenon where a structural element subjected to twisting ([torsional](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torsion_(mechanics))) forces undergoes sudden deformation or failure beyond a critical [torque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torque) threshold.

definition: Total external reflection is a phenomenon traditionally involving [X-rays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X-rays) and [extreme ultraviolet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extreme_ultraviolet), but in principle any type of electromagnetic or other wave, closely related to [total internal reflection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_internal_reflection).

total position-spread (TPS) [tensor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tensor) is a quantity originally introduced in the modern theory of [electrical conductivity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrical_conductivity).
Touschek effect describes the scattering and loss of charged particles in a [storage ring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Storage_ring).

Townsend discharge or Townsend avalanche is an [ionisation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ionisation) process for [gas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gas)es where free [electron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron)s are accelerated by an [electric field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_field), collide with gas molecules, and consequently free additional electrons.
toy model is a deliberately simplistic model with many details removed so that it can be used to explain a mechanism concisely.
TRACE is a high-precision [orbit determination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orbit_determination) and orbit propagation program.

trace distance is a [metric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metric_(mathematics)) on the space of [density matrices](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Density_matrix) and gives a measure of the distinguishability between two states.

Track Imaging Cherenkov Experiment (TrICE) is a ground-based [cosmic ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cosmic_ray) telescope located at [Argonne National Laboratory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argonne_National_Laboratory) near [Chicago, IL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago,_IL).

Track significance, in [high energy collision](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Particle_physics) [experiment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Experiment)s, is defined as the [ratio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ratio) between the [impact parameter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impact_parameter) of a track (distance from the primary vertex) and the estimated error in it.
tracking == Principles of Track Reconstruction == Tracking is based on the interaction of charged particles with a detector material.
TrackingPoint is an applied technology company based in [Austin, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin,_Texas).

tractrix (; plural: tractrices) is the [curve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curve) along which an object moves, under the influence of [friction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friction), when pulled on a [horizontal plane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horizontal_plane) by a [line segment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Line_segment) attached to a pulling point (the tractor) that moves at a [right angle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right_angle) to the initial line between the object and the puller at an [infinitesimal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infinitesimal) speed.
