definition: trans-Planckian problem is the problem of the appearance of quantities beyond the [Planck scale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planck_scale), which raise doubts on the physical validity of some results in these two areas, since one expects the physical laws to suffer radical modifications beyond the Planck scale.

transfer-matrix method is a [mathematical technique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_physics) which is used to write the [partition function](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partition_function_(mathematics)) into a simpler form.

transfer-matrix method is a method used in [optics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optics) and [acoustics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acoustics) to analyze the propagation of [electromagnetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electromagnetic_wave) or [acoustic wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acoustic_wave)s through a [stratified medium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stratified_medium) — a stack of [thin film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thin_film)s.

Transition radiation (TR) is a form of [electromagnetic radiation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electromagnetic_radiation) emitted when a [charged particle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charged_particle) passes through [[Homogeneity and heterogeneity#Heterogeneity|inhomogeneous]] media, such as a boundary between two different media.

Translation Confinement Sustainment experiment (TCS) was a plasma physics experiment at the [University of Washington's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Washington) Redmond Plasma Physics Laboratory from 2002 until 2009.

translation operator is defined as an [operator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operator_(physics)) which shifts particles and [fields](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Field_(physics)) by a certain amount in a certain direction.

transmission coefficient is used in [physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physics) and [electrical engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrical_engineering) when [wave propagation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wave_propagation) in a medium containing [discontinuities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discontinuity_(mathematics)) is considered.

transparency (also called pellucidity or diaphaneity) is the [physical property](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physical_property) of allowing [light](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Light) to pass through the material without appreciable [scattering of light](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Light_scattering_by_particles).

Transpiration cooling is a thermodynamic process where [cooling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cooling) is achieved by a process of moving a liquid or a gas through the wall of a structure to absorb some portion of the [heat energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internal_energy) from the structure while simultaneously [actively](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Active_cooling) reducing the [convective](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convection_(heat_transfer)) and [radiative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radiative_heat_transfer) ==See also== *

Transposition is the periodic swapping of positions of the conductors of a [transmission line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transmission_line), in order to reduce [crosstalk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crosstalk) and otherwise improve transmission.

transverse mass is a useful quantity to define for use in [particle physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Particle_physics) as it is invariant under [Lorentz boost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lorentz_boost) along the z direction.

transverse momentum distributions (TMDs) are the distributions of the hadron's [quark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quark) or [gluon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gluon) [momenta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Momentum) that are perpendicular to the [momentum transfer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Momentum_transfer) between the beam and the hadron.
transverse field Ising model is a quantum version of the classical [Ising model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ising_model).
trapped-ion quantum computer (TIQC) is one proposed approach to a large-scale [quantum computer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_computer).
Trevor Evans (26 April 1927 — 10 October 2010) was a British physical scientist who specialised in the properties of [diamonds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diamond).

trihydrogen cation or protonated molecular hydrogen ([IUPAC name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IUPAC_nomenclature_of_inorganic_chemistry): hydrogen[onium ion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Onium_ion)) is a [cation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cation) (positive [ion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ion)) with [formula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_formula) , consisting of three [hydrogen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrogen) nuclei ([proton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proton)s) sharing two [electron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron)s.

Tsai–Wu failure criterion is a phenomenological [material failure theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Material_failure_theory) which is widely used for anisotropic [composite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Composite_material) materials which have different strengths in tension and compression.
Tsallis entropy is a generalization of the standard [Boltzmann–Gibbs entropy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entropy_(statistical_thermodynamics)).
Tsirelson bound is an upper limit to quantum mechanical correlations between distant events.
Tube-based nanostructures are [nanolattices](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanolattices) made of connected tubes and exhibit nanoscale organization above the molecular level.

TUM School of Natural Sciences (NAT) is a school of the [Technical University of Munich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Technical_University_of_Munich), established in 2022 by the merger of various former departments.
tune shift with amplitude is an important concept in circular [accelerators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Particle_accelerator) or [synchrotron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synchrotron)s.

Tunnel injection is a [field electron emission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Field_electron_emission) effect; specifically a quantum process called [Fowler–Nordheim tunneling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fowler–Nordheim_tunneling), whereby [charge carrier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charge_carrier)s are injected to an electric conductor through a thin layer of an electric insulator.

tunnel ionization is a process in which [electron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron)s in an [atom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atom) (or a [molecule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecule)) [tunnel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_tunnelling) through the potential barrier and escape from the atom (or molecule).
tunnel junction is a barrier, such as a thin insulating layer or electric potential, between two electrically conducting materials.
Tuorla Observatory is the Department of Astronomy at the [University of Turku](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Turku), southwest [Finland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finland).

Turbidity is the cloudiness or [haziness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haze) of a [fluid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fluid) caused by large numbers of individual [particles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Particle_(ecology)) that are generally invisible to the [naked eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naked_eye).

turbulence or turbulent flow is [fluid motion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fluid_motion) exhibiting [chaotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaos_theory) changes in [pressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pressure) and [flow velocity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flow_velocity).

Turkish Journal of Physics is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) published bimonthly by [Scientific and Technological Research Council of Turkey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_and_Technological_Research_Council_of_Turkey) (TÜBİTAK).

definition: Twisted geometries are [discrete geometries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discrete_geometry) that play a role in [loop quantum gravity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loop_quantum_gravity) and spin foam models, where they appear in the semiclassical limit of [spin networks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin_networks).

twistor correspondence (also known as Penrose–Ward correspondence) is a [bijection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bijection) between [instantons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instantons) on [complexified](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complexification) [Minkowski space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minkowski_space) and [holomorphic vector bundle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holomorphic_vector_bundle)s on [twistor space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twistor_space), which as a [complex manifold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex_manifold) is also known as the ADHM construction, hence giving a classification of instantons.
twistor theory was proposed by [Roger Penrose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Penrose) in 1967 * [http://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/lmason/Tn/ Twistor newsletter] archives.

two capacitor paradox or capacitor paradox is a [paradox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paradox), or counterintuitive [thought experiment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thought_experiment), in [electric circuit theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circuit_theory).
two-balloon experiment is an experiment involving interconnected [balloon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balloon)s.
two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) is a [scientific model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_model) in [solid-state physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solid-state_physics).
two-dimensional semiconductor (also known as 2D semiconductor) is a type of natural [semiconductor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semiconductor) with thicknesses on the atomic scale.

two-electron atom or helium-like ion is a [quantum mechanical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanical) system consisting of one [nucleus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_nucleus) with a [charge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrical_charge) of Z[e](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elementary_charge) and just two [electron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron)s.
two-Higgs-doublet model (2HDM) is an extension of the [Standard Model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_Model) of [particle physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Particle_physics).

definition: two-photon absorption (TPA or 2PA), also called two-photon excitation or non-linear absorption, is the simultaneous [absorption](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absorption_(electromagnetic_radiation)) of two [photon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photon)s of identical or different frequencies in order to [excite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron_excitation) an [atom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atom) or a [molecule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecule) from one state (usually the [ground state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ground_state)), via a virtual [energy level](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy_level), to a higher energy, most commonly an [excited electronic state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Excited_electronic_state).

definition: Two-photon physics, also called gamma–gamma physics, is a branch of [particle physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Particle_physics) that describes the [interaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fundamental_interaction)s between two [photons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photons).

two-state system (also known as a two-level system) is a [quantum system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_system) that can exist in any [quantum superposition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_superposition) of two independent (physically distinguishable) [quantum state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_state)s.

two-state vector formalism (TSVF) is a description of [quantum mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics) in terms of a [causal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Causality) relation in which the present is caused by quantum states of the past and of the future taken in combination.

Tyndall Medal is a prize from the [Institute of Acoustics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institute_of_Acoustics_(United_Kingdom)) awarded every two years to a citizen of the UK, preferably under the age of 40, for [[Category:Physics awards]] [[Category:British science and technology awards]] 9fo6yxtgw9w63cdzwahyhzalejgpicp
Tyndall's bar breaker is a physical demonstration experiment to demonstrate the forces created by thermal expansion and shrinkage.

type I supergravity is the theory of [supergravity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supergravity) in ten [dimension](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dimension)s with a single [supercharge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supercharge).

type IIA supergravity is the unique [supergravity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supergravity) in ten [dimension](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dimension)s with two [supercharge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supercharge)s of opposite [chirality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chirality_(physics)).

type IIB supergravity is the unique [supergravity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supergravity) in ten [dimension](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dimension)s with two [supercharge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supercharge)s of the same [chirality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chirality_(physics)).

u-bit or ubit is a proposed theoretical entity which arises in attempts to reformulate [wave functions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wave_functions) using only [real number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_number)s instead of the [complex number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex_number)s conventionally used.
Udwadia–Kalaba formulation is a method for deriving the equations of motion of a constrained [mechanical system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mechanical_system).

Uehling potential describes the interaction potential between two electric charges which, in addition to the classical [Coulomb potential](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coulomb_potential), contains an extra term responsible for the electric [polarization of the vacuum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vacuum_polarization).
UK Molecular R-Matrix codes are a set of software routines used to calculate the effects of collision of electrons with atoms and molecules.

ultradivided matter is a family of [states of matter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_of_matter) characterised by a heterogeneous mixture of two or more different materials, where the [interaction energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interaction_energy) between the suspended phase is larger than kT.

ultramicroscope is a [microscope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microscope) with a system that lights the object in a way that allows viewing of tiny [particle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Particle)s via [light scattering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Light_scattering), and not [light reflection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reflection_(physics)) or [absorption](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absorption_(electromagnetic_radiation)).

ultrasound research interface (URI) is a software tool loaded onto a diagnostic clinical ultrasound device which provides functionality beyond typical clinical modes of operation.

ultraviolet completion, or UV completion, of a [quantum field theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_field_theory) is the passing from a lower energy [quantum field theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_field_theory) to a more general quantum field theory above a threshold value known as the [cutoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cutoff_(physics)).

ultraviolet divergence or UV divergence is a situation in which an [integral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Integral), for example a [Feynman diagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feynman_diagram), diverges because of contributions of objects with unbounded [energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy), or, equivalently, because of physical phenomena at infinitesimal distances.

Umkehr (meaning 'reversal', , ) is the time variation of the ratio of the scattered intensity at two different wavelengths.

Uncertainty or incertitude refers to situations involving imperfect or unknown [information](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Information).

UNESCO Niels Bohr Medal was first minted in 1985 to commemorate the 100th anniversary of the birth of the Danish nuclear physicist [Niels Bohr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niels_Bohr).

unextendible product basis is a set of orthogonal, non-[entangled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_entanglement) [state vectors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_state) for a multipartite system, with the property that [local operations and classical communication](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LOCC) are insufficient to distinguish one member of the set from the others.

Unification of theories about [observable fundamental phenomena of nature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fundamental_interaction) is one of the primary goals of [physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physics).

unified field theory (UFT) is a type of [field theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Field_theory_(physics)) that allows all [fundamental forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fundamental_forces) of nature, including gravity, and all [elementary particle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elementary_particle)s to be written in terms of a single physical [field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Field_(physics)).

uniform theory of diffraction (UTD) is a [high-frequency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_frequency) method for solving [electromagnetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electromagnetic_radiation) [scattering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scattering) problems from electrically small discontinuities or discontinuities in more than one dimension at the same point.

UNIQUAC (a [portmanteau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portmanteau) of universal quasichemical) is an [activity coefficient](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Activity_coefficient) model used in description of [phase equilibria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phase_equilibria).

unit vector in a [normed vector space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normed_vector_space) is a [vector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vector_(mathematics_and_physics)) (often a [spatial vector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vector_(geometry))) of [length](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norm_(mathematics)) 1.

unitarity (process) is the condition that the time evolution of a [quantum state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_state) according to the [Schrödinger equation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schrödinger_equation) is mathematically represented by a [unitary operator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unitary_operator).

unitary modular tensor category is a certain type of [algebraic structure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algebraic_structure), defined by equipping a [modular tensor category](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modular_tensor_category) with additional data that reflects the principle of [unitarity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unitarity_(physics)) in quantum mechanics.

United Kingdom patent 394325 Improvements in and relating to Sound-transmission, Sound-recording and Sound-reproducing Systems is a fundamental work on stereophonic sound, written by [Alan Blumlein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Blumlein) in 1931 and published in 1933.

United States Physics Olympiad (USAPhO) is a [high school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_school) [physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physics) [competition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Student_competition) run by the [American Association of Physics Teachers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Association_of_Physics_Teachers) and the [American Institute of Physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Institute_of_Physics) to select the team to represent the United States at the [International Physics Olympiad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Physics_Olympiad) (IPhO).
Universal causation is the [proposition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proposition) that everything in the universe has a cause and is thus an effect of that cause.

Universal conductance fluctuations (UCF) in [mesoscopic physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesoscopic_physics) is a phenomenon encountered in electrical transport experiments in [mesoscopic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesoscopic_physics) species.
universal dielectric response, or UDR, refers to the observed emergent behaviour of the [dielectric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dielectric) properties exhibited by diverse solid state systems.
universal extra dimensions include one or more spatial dimensions beyond the three spatial and one temporal dimensions that are observed.

universal wavefunction or the wavefunction of the universe is the [wavefunction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wavefunction) or [quantum state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_state) of the entire [universe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universe).

unparticle physics is a speculative theory that conjectures a form of [matter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matter) that cannot be explained in terms of [particles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elementary_particle) using the [Standard Model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_Model) of particle physics, because its components are [scale invariant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scale_invariance).

Unruh–DeWitt detector is an idealized phenomenological model of a localized [quantum probe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_measurement) used to operationalize the measurement of particles in curved or dynamical [spacetime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spacetime)s.

Vacuum energy is an underlying background [energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy) that exists in [space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space) throughout the entire [universe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universe).

vacuum expectation value (VEV) of an [operator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operator_(physics)) is its average or [expectation value](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expectation_value_(quantum_mechanics)) in the [vacuum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vacuum_state).

vacuum level refers to the energy of a free stationary [electron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron) that is outside of any material (it is in a perfect [vacuum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vacuum)).

definition: Vafa–Witten theorem, named after [Cumrun Vafa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cumrun_Vafa) and [Edward Witten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Witten), is a [theorem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theorem) that shows that vector-like [global symmetries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_symmetry) (those that transform as expected under reflections) such as [isospin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isospin) and [baryon number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baryon_number) in vector-like gauge theories like [quantum chromodynamics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_chromodynamics) cannot be [spontaneously broken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spontaneous_symmetry_breaking) as long as the [theta angle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theta_vacuum) is zero.

valence bond (VB) theory is one of the two basic theories, along with [molecular orbital (MO) theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_orbital_theory), that were developed to use the methods of [quantum mechanics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_mechanics) to describe [chemical bond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_bond)ing.

Van Allen radiation belt is a zone of [energetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy) [charged particle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charged_particle)s, most of which originate from [solar wind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_wind), that are captured and held around a planet by that planet's [magnetosphere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnetosphere).

Van de Graaff generator is an [electrostatic generator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrostatic_generator) which uses a moving belt to accumulate [electric charge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_charge) on a hollow metal globe on the top of an insulated column, creating very high [electric potential](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_potential)s.

Van Laar equation is a [thermodynamic activity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thermodynamic_activity) model, which was developed by [Johannes van Laar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannes_van_Laar) in 1910-1913, to describe [phase equilibria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phase_equilibria) of liquid mixtures.

van Stockum dust or the Lanczos–van Stockum dust is an exact solution of the [Einstein field equations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Einstein_field_equations) where the gravitational field is generated by [dust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dust_solution) rotating about an axis of cylindrical symmetry.

Van Vleck paramagnetism refers to a positive and [temperature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temperature)-independent contribution to the [magnetic susceptibility](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnetic_susceptibility) of a material, derived from second order corrections to the [Zeeman interaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zeeman_effect).

Vanishing-dimensions theory is a [particle physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Particle_physics) theory suggesting that systems with higher energy have a smaller number of [dimensions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dimension_(mathematics_and_physics)).

Vapor pressure or equilibrium vapor pressure is the [pressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pressure) exerted by a [vapor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vapor) in [thermodynamic equilibrium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thermodynamic_equilibrium) with its [condensed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Condensation) [phase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phase_(matter))s (solid or liquid) at a given temperature in a [[thermodynamic system#Closed system|closed system]].

variational method is one way of finding [approximation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Approximation)s to the lowest energy eigenstate or [ground state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ground_state), and some excited states.

variational Monte Carlo (VMC) is a [quantum Monte Carlo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_Monte_Carlo) method that applies the [variational method](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variational_method_(quantum_mechanics)) to approximate the [ground state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ground_state) of a quantum system.

variational principle is a mathematical procedure that renders a physical problem solvable by the [calculus of variations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calculus_of_variations), which concerns finding functions that optimize the values of quantities that depend on those functions.

variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) is a [quantum algorithm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_algorithm) for [quantum chemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_chemistry), [quantum simulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantum_simulation)s and [optimization problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optimization_problem)s.

varifocal lens is a [camera lens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camera_lens) with variable [focal length](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Focal_length) in which [focus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Focus_(optics)) changes as focal length (and [magnification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnification)) changes, as compared to a [parfocal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parfocal_lens) ( ==See also== * [Zoom lens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zoom_lens) * [Parfocal lens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parfocal_lens) * [Prime lens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_lens) * [Autofocus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autofocus) * [Camera lens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camera_lens) * [Progressive lens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressive_lens) (ophthalmic) ==References== [[Category:Optics]] ==Further read

zero-energy universe hypothesis proposes that the total amount of [energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy) in the [universe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universe) is exactly [zero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zero): its amount of positive energy in the form of [matter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matter) is exactly canceled out by its [negative energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Negative_energy) in the form of [gravity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gravity).
